MOURNING THE DEATH OF MILO DAKIN. WHEREAS, the Alabama Legislature is deeply saddened upon the death of Milo Dakin at 4:40 p.m., February 10, 2003; and WHEREAS, Milo Dakin was born on February 22, 1941, in Grant Parish, Louisiana; he served in the United States Army and embarked upon a career in journalism in his native state, culminating in his assuming positions in political reportage with “The Mont­ gomery Advertiser” in 1968, then “The Atlanta Constitution” in 1972; and WHEREAS, in 1974 Milo became Public Information Of­ ficer, then Chief of Staff for longtime Georgia Speaker of the House Tom Murphy, serving with the Speaker for four years; and WHEREAS, in 1978 Milo returned to Montgomery to estab­ lish a position in governmental affairs, eventually establishing his own business, The Dakin Group, whose activities extended to almost every Southern capital as well as Washington, D. C.; and WHEREAS, Milo Dakin was highly respected as a forthright and effective lobbyist, and for his personal attributes of honesty, loyalty, keen intellect, and willingness to help all who sought his friendship, advice, and counsel; and WHEREAS, a man of many and varied interests, Milo was often consulted for his knowledge of history, geography, photo­ graphy, and antiques, as well as his culinary prowess and his deep de­ votion to all things pertaining to his beloved Louisiana State Uni- versity Tigers; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA­ BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That we mourn the passing of Milo Dakin and pay tribute to his life as a friend and associate and to his many contributions to Alabama. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That in testimony of the esteem in which he is held by the Alabama Legislature, we hereby direct that copies of this resolution be prepared for Milo Dakin’s wife, Betsy Hodde Dakin; his son, William Paul Hodde Dakin; his daughter, Dana Kimberlie Dakin Hill; his grandchildren, Dakin and Will Braden Hill; his sister, Loretta O’Bannon; his brother, Russell Dakin; and for his loyal and bereaved staff and associates at The Da­ kin Group. Senator Little (T) requested and received unanimous consent REGULAR SESSION 201 5th Day - March 14, 2003 to suspend the provisions of Senate Rule 55 and the Resolution was adopted by the Senate.

COMMENDING THE AWARENESS PROGRAM, ALABAMA OPERATION LIFESAVER. WHEREAS, we recognize and highly commend Alabama Operation Lifesaver, a nonprofit education and awareness program dedicated to preventing accidents at rail-highway grade crossings and accidents involving trespassers on railroad right-of-ways; and WHEREAS, Alabama Operation Lifesaver endeavors to ac­ complish its mission by promoting the “3 E’s,” education, enforce­ ment, and engineering; and WHEREAS, Alabama Operation Lifesaver strives to educate the public with regard to the good safety practices which should be used when approaching railroad crossings and with regard to the dangers inherent in trespassing on railroad right-of-ways; and WHEREAS, Alabama Operation Lifesaver encourages con­ tinued engineering research and innovation to improve the safety of railroad crossings; and WHEREAS, the Operation Lifesaver Program has been func­ tioning in Alabama since 1976, and since its inception, it has been supported and sustained by the railroads of Alabama; and WHEREAS, Operation Lifesaver’s critical safety programs are presented to school children, driver’s education students, business leaders, law enforcement personnel and other emergency responders, REGULAR SESSION 314 8th Day - April 1, 2003 truck drivers, and bus drivers, including school bus drivers, through­ out the state by a group of dedicated volunteers which includes loco­ motive engineer and other railroad employees, teachers, law enforce- ment officers, retirees, truck drivers, students, and others from virtu­ ally all walks of life; and WHEREAS, there has been a downward trend in the number of accidents at railroad crossings since Operation Lifesaver’s incep­ tion in Alabama, and in the four year period from 1998 through 2001, the number of railroad crossing accidents decreased almost 30%; and WHEREAS, many lives have been saved and many injuries have been prevented thanks to the efforts of Alabama Operation Life­ saver; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA­ BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That Ala­ bama Operation Lifesaver, State Coordinator Nancy Hudson, the Op- eration Lifesaver volunteers, and the Alabama railroads are hereby commended for their exemplary and successful efforts to prevent accidents at railroad crossing and accidents involving trespassers on railroad right-of-ways, and a copy of this resolution shall be provided for appropriate presentation with sincere tribute. EMPHASIZING THE IMPORTANCE OF THE ROLE OF PARENTS AND GUARDIANS AS CAREGIVERS FOR DISABLED CHILDREN DURING CERTAIN COMPETITIVE EVENTS. WHEREAS, the role of parents and guardians in the oversight and care of disabled children is critical to the well-being of such children; and WHEREAS, when disabled children attend competitions such as the Alabama Special Olympics, they are sometimes required to be accommodated at dormitories on publicly-owned properties, such as college and university campuses; and WHEREAS, the separation of disabled children from their parents or guardians at such competitive events may lead to an erosion of the critically important parent and child bond and may otherwise adversely affect the child; indeed, the well-being of these children may best be served by having the child remain with their parents or guardians during these times; and WHEREAS, the practice of using state properties for the feeding, housing, and transportation of disabled children at such REGULAR SESSION 330 8th Day - April 1, 2003 events may also interfere with the inherent rights of parents and guardians as caretakers; and WHEREAS, the organizations and hosts of such competitions for disabled children could use waivers of liability and other legal agreements to allow parents and children to be together at such events, a better solution than the current all or nothing policy from which parents are forced to chose; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA­ BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That by copy of this resolution, we urge the governing authorities of the Alabama Special Olympics, other competition sponsors, disability advocacy groups, and participating colleges and universities to adopt policies that allow parents and guardians to provide parental care and over­ sight of their disabled children at competitive events, except during those times that the children are actually participating in those events. Senator Denton requested and received unanimous consent to suspend the provisions of Senate Rule 55 and the Resolution was adopted by the Senate.

NAMING WALLACE STATE COMMUNITY COLLEGE IN HANCEVILLE, ALABAMA, JAMES C. BAILEY STATE COLLEGE. WHEREAS, Wallace State Community College, located in Hanceville, Alabama, was originally named George C. Wallace State Trade School of Cullman County when created by the Legislature in 1963; and WHEREAS, eight years after the college was created, on Feb­ ruary 16, 1971, Dr. James C. (Jake) Bailey was appointed President, and during the first year of his presidency, on December 6, 1971, the college received accreditation by the Southern Association of Col­ leges and Schools; and WHEREAS, during Dr. Bailey’s 32 years as President of the college, the college has grown from 10 programs housed in 3 build­ ings on 20 acres of land to more than 100 career options offered in 35-plus buildings on property covering 250 acres, and enrollment has escalated from 69 to 7,000 students; and WHEREAS, announcing his retirement on April 1, 2003, effective April 30, Dr. Bailey will leave the college in Hanceville academically strong, athletically competitive, and in excellent finan­ cial health with surplus funds; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA­ BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That on April 30, 2003, the name of Wallace State Community College, lo­ cated in Hanceville, Alabama, shall be changed to James C. Bailey State College. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the educational institu­ tion known as Wallace State Community College shall remain an educational institution under the name of James C. Bailey State College, and by that name may have and exercise all powers pre­ viously enjoyed by Wallace State Community College and shall suc­ ceed to all the rights, privileges, obligations, liabilities, emoluments, REGULAR SESSION 523 12th Day - April 15, 2003 benefits, interests, and titles at any time vested in the institution in its respective names. None of the powers, authority, obligations, lia­ bilities, or functions of the institution shall be abated or impaired by this resolution. Only the name of the institution shall be changed by this resolution. Whenever the institution is referred to in the consti­ tution, laws, rules, or regulations of this state, or any instrumentality of this state, by any one of the respective names by which it has been known, the same shall be considered to refer to James C. Bailey State College. Senator Little (Z) requested and received unanimous consent to suspend the provisions of Senate Rule 55 and the Resolution was adopted by the Senate.

COMMENDING MR. AND MRS. MANSELL GARRETT JR., ON THE OCCASION OF THEIR 50TH WEDD­ ING ANNIVERSARY. WHEREAS, heartiest congratulations are herein extended to Mr. and Mrs. Mansell Garrett, Jr., on the occasion of their 50th Wedding Anniversary on June 22, 2003; and WHEREAS, Mansell Raymond and Helen McClain Garrett will be joined by family and friends at a gala reception at the First United Methodist Church in Leeds, Alabama, on June 22, 2003; and WHEREAS, Mansell Garrett, Jr., is a graduate of Leeds High School and served his country in the Korean Conflict with the 45th Infantry Division; during his 30-year career as a postal carrier in Leeds, he also has been involved in the Boy Scouts of America from 1974 to 1982, an active member of the First United Methodist Church of Leeds and the Leeds Centennial Committee; and WHEREAS, Helen Garrett is a graduate of Ensley High School and Alabama Polytechnic Institute, now Auburn University; she has been an educator at Leeds High School for 33 years, cheerleader sponsor from 1955 to 1962, faculty sponsor of both the high school’s Birmingham Veterans’ Day Parade float from 1967 to 1975 and the Future Homemakers of America, and an active member of the First United Methodist Church of Leeds; and WHEREAS, through the years of their long and happy lives together, the commitment of this fine couple to the ideals of marriage has not only enriched their lives, but also the lives of their family and others who have witnessed their devotion to each other; now therefore, 780 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2003 23rd Day - June 9, 2003 BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA­ BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That sincere commendation is herein extended to Mr. and Mrs. Mansell Garrett, Jr., on the celebration of their 50th Wedding Anniversary and it is directed that they receive a copy of this resolution with warm best wishes for many more happy years together. Senator Barron requested and received unanimous consent to suspend the provisions of Senate Rule 55 and the Resolution was adopted by the Senate.

to wit: SUBSTITUTE FOR HB209 A BILL TO BE ENTITLED AN ACT Relating to the City of Montgomery, to rename a portion of Jackson Street as Martin Luther King, Jr. Avenue in honor of his dis­ tinguished service to the Civil Rights Movement. BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALABAMA: Section 1. In honor and recognition of the significant contri­ butions and achievements of Martin Luther King, Jr. to the Civil Rights Movement, that portion of the existing Jackson Street in the City of Montgomery, Alabama, located south of Adams Avenue is hereby renamed “Martin Luther King, Jr. Avenue.” That portion of the existing Jackson Avenue located north of Adams Avenue shall continue to be named Jackson Avenue. Section 2. This act shall become effective immediately fol­ lowing its passage and approval by the Governor, or its otherwise be­ coming law. Which was adopted.

COMMENDING DR. KENNETH A. WILLIAMS ON HIS OUTSTANDING PROFESSIONAL ACHIEVEMENTS. WHEREAS, heartiest congratulations are herein extended to Dr. Kenneth A. Williams on his outstanding professional achieve­ ments; and WHEREAS, Kenneth Williams is the son of Sue Moore of Montgomery; he attended Forest Avenue Elementary School, Clo­ verdale Junior High School, and Sidney Lanier High School; and WHEREAS, Kenneth Williams attended Georgia Institute of Technology under a Lockheed scholarship, where he received a Bachelor of Science Degree and Master’s Degree in Mechanical En­ gineering; he later earned a Ph.D. in Mechanical Engineering from the University of New Mexico; and WHEREAS, Kenneth Williams worked for two years with General Atomic in San Diego before joining Los Alamos National Laboratory where he was in advanced computational fluid dynamic research for 10 years; in 1984 Mr. Williams began his 10-year career with Science Applications International Corporation where he was Senior Vice President; in 1994 he began his own company and is pre­ sently co-owner of the engineering software company, Arena-flow; and WHEREAS, Dr. Williams received the 2003 Howard Taylor Award for his research paper “Process Modeling: Sand Core Blow­ ing” in recognition of research having the greatest long range tech­ nical significance in the field of cast metals technology; this award was presented at the Divisional Awards Luncheon at the 107th Casting Congress in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, in April 2003; and WHEREAS, Kenneth and his wife, Lori Ann Williams, now reside in Albuquerque, New Mexico, and are the proud parents of two sons; the older son lives in Berkeley, California, and works as a geophysicist and the younger son is a junior in high school; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA­ BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That we hereby most highly commend Dr. Kenneth A. Williams, a native of 1300 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2003 26th Day - June 12, 2003 Montgomery, Alabama, upon his outstanding professional achieve­ ments and do further direct that a copy of this resolution be provided to him with our sincere best wishes for all future endeavors. Senator Dixon requested and received unanimous consent to suspend the provisions of Senate Rule 55 and the Resolution was adopted by the Senate.

To provide for a limitation of civil liability for a farmer who permits another to enter property under the farmer’s control for the purpose of removing remaining crops. The Standing Committee on Judiciary reported the following substitute for the Bill, HB41, to wit: SUBSTITUTE FOR HB41 A BILL TO BE ENTITLED AN ACT To provide for a limitation of civil liability for a farmer who permits an individual employed by or who is an agent of a nonprofit entity to enter property under the farmer’s control for the purpose of removing remaining crops. BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALABAMA: Section 1. Notwithstanding any law to the contrary, any farm­ er, as an owner, lessee, occupant, or person otherwise in control of land, who allows without compensation another person who is employed by or who is an agent of a nonprofit entity to enter upon the land for the purpose of removing any crops remaining in the farmer’s fields following the harvesting of the crops, owes that person the same duty of care the farmer owes a trespasser. For purposes of this section a nonprofit entity is an entity that is exempt from federal income tax under 26 U.S.C. Section 501(c)(3). Section 2. This act shall become effective on the first day of the third month following its passage and approval by the Governor, or its otherwise becoming law. Which was adopted.

MOURNING THE DEATH OF MR. CHARLES MOLTON WILLIAMS OF BIRMINGHAM, ALABAMA. WHEREAS, the Alabama Legislature is deeply saddened at the death of Mr. Charles Molton Williams of Birmingham, Alabama, on January 6, 2004, at the age of 73 years; and WHEREAS, born June 21, 1930, in Birmingham, Mr. Will- iams received a Bachelor of Science Degree in Business Administra- tion from Washington and Lee University in 1952; he later joined the business founded by his grandfather and became President of Molton, Allen, and Williams, Inc., in 1968 and Chairman of the Board in 1978; he was the founding Chairman of Brigham-Williams and As- sociates, Inc., which later became RealtySouth; and WHEREAS, deeply involved in prison ministry, Mr. Will- iams was a member of South Highland Presbyterian Church for over 50 years and founded Re-Entry Ministries, Inc., an outreach program that assists ex-inmates; he also served as Chairman and Chief Exec- utive Officer of Cornerstone Schools of Alabama, Inc., which offers religious oriented education to inner-city children; and WHEREAS, some of the numerous civic activities of Mr. Williams include membership in the Downtown Kiwanis Club, and leadership positions with the Birmingham Festival of Arts Associa- tion; the Baptist Hospitals Advisory Board; Boys and Girls Clubs of Central Alabama, Inc.; the Salvation Army Advisory Board; Impact Family Counseling, Inc.; and Kairos; he also was a member of the Country Club of Birmingham, The Club, and the Redstone Club; and WHEREAS, left to cherish the memory of Molton Williams are his devoted wife, Hope; children, Charles M. Williams, Jr. (Kath- leen); J. T. Hunter Williams (Gini); John W. Williams (Beth); and Kate Hope Williams Simpson (Charles); grandchildren, Claire Eve- lyn Williams; Charles Molton Williams, III; Thomas Hunter Molton Williams; Donald Porter Williams; John White Williams, Jr.; Mari- anne Coston Williams; Hope White Simpson; Charles Hatcher Sim- pson, Jr.; and Samuel Day Simpson; and WHEREAS, the illustrious record of Charles Molton Will- iams’s personal, public, and civic achievements have indeed earned for him the respect of his family, friends, and the community; now therefore, 124 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2004 2nd Day - February 5, 2004 BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That in sad- ness and regret the death of Mr. Charles Molton Williams of Bir- mingham, Alabama, is hereby recorded and deepest sympathy is extended to his wife for whom a copy of this resolution shall be pro- vided. Senator French requested and received unanimous consent to suspend the provisions of Senate Rule 55 and the Resolution was adopted by the Senate.

HONORING THE LIFE AND SERVICE OF MR. BILL ROPER OF MONTGOMERY, ALABAMA. WHEREAS, recorded with deep and abiding sorrow is the la- mentable death of Mr. Bill Roper, Minister of Music for First Baptist Church in Montgomery, Alabama, on January 24, 2004, at the age of 66 years; and WHEREAS, with his sincere dedication and love for music, Mr. Roper served his Lord and Savior Jesus Christ as Minister of Mu- sic at First Baptist Church for 32 years, and as director and creator of the annual Living Christmas Tree program for 23 years, his trium- phant and beautiful musical presentations were attended by countless individuals from near and far; and WHEREAS, as Minister of Music of the Sanctuary Choir, membership increased from 50 to 164 and, with his God-given talents and musical abilities, he created the School of Fine Arts at First Bap- tist Church in 1984, which offers lessons in numerous and varied mu- sical programs, including voice, piano, organ, and guitar; and 132 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2004 2nd Day - February 5, 2004 WHEREAS, Mr. Roper often used affirming references to faith and God in his conversations and offered immense pleasure to church members and visitors at First Baptist Church by selecting hymns and songs for individuals of all ages and walks of life; and WHEREAS, left to cherish the precious memory of Mr. Bill Roper are his devoted wife of 42 years, Patty Phillips Roper; daugh- ters, Beth (Benjy) Harris and Kathy (Mike) Shirley; four grandchil- dren; a sister; and other close family members and friends; now there- fore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That, in praise and gratitude, we hereby honor the life and service of Mr. Bill Roper, Minister of Music at First Baptist Church in Montgomery, Al- abama, who will live forever in the hearts and minds of all those whose lives he touched, and extend heartfelt sympathy to his wife, for whom a copy of this resolution is provided that she may know of our shared sorrow in her great and inconsolable loss. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That a copy of this resolu- tion be presented to Dr. Jay Wolf, Pastor, First Baptist Church, Mont- gomery, Alabama, for appropriate display. HONORING THE LIFE AND SERVICE OF THE LATE SHERIFF C. F. “NEIL” GRANTHAM OF COFFEE COUN- TY, ALABAMA. 330 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2004 8th Day - February 26, 2004 WHEREAS, Sheriff C. F. “Neil” Grantham will be honored posthumously by his family and many friends on March 1, 2004, the 25th anniversary of his death, at the Old Coffee County Jail in Elba, Alabama, as a worthy exemplar, caring and dedicated, who stood ev- er ready to provide prompt and professional response to the citizens of Coffee County; and WHEREAS, Sheriff Grantham began his first term as sheriff in January 1975 and, after being reelected, ably began his second term in January 1979, when, tragically, he was killed outside of the sheriff’s office 45 days later on March 1, 1979; and WHEREAS, during his distinguished tenure, Sheriff Gran- tham’s sense of duty and dedication in defense of others represented the ultimate in personal sacrifice and his devotion to duty, personal integrity, outgoing personality, and ability to relate to others fostered a spirit of friendship, respect, and trust among his fellow officers; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That we rec- ognize with gratitude and praise the life and service of the late Sheriff C. F. “Neil” Grantham, which is shared with his beloved family, fel- low officers, and many, many friends. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That a copy of this resolu- tion be provided during the Memorial Service for Sheriff C. F. “Neil” Grantham on March 1, 2004, as an expression of our thanks to God for his life and service with the Coffee County Sheriff’s Office, and our shared sorrow in his loss. EXPRESSING GRATITUDE TO MRS. JUNE WEAVER FOR EXEMPLARY SERVICE TO THE LEGISLA- TURE OF ALABAMA. WHEREAS, with utmost respect and highest regard, we rec- ognize the exemplary service of Mrs. June Weaver to the Legislature of Alabama and the citizens of this state; and WHEREAS, from 1991 to 2003, Mrs. Weaver was employed with the Legislative Reference Service as a proofreader, an indis- pensable behind-the-scenes staff member seldom seen in the cham- bers, but whose endless efforts and uncompromising commitment to quality and correctness were essential components in ensuring both excellence and efficiency in the legislative process; and WHEREAS, as a former English and Drama teacher, June earnestly employed her language proficiency, grammatical skills, and well-read knowledge in multiple ways that help guarantee correctly REGULAR SESSION 343 8th Day - February 26, 2004 crafted statutes, resolutions, administrative rules, and legal opinions; indeed, her dedication, dependability, and work ethic constitute ex- ceptional public service; and WHEREAS, June Weaver’s contributions to the maintenance of the Code of Alabama 1975, is noteworthy; proofreading these laws is a thankless task that can easily result in a self-inflicted coma; how- ever, with pride, patience, and persistence she helped ensure that the codification process was accurate and timely available; and WHEREAS, co-workers are especially fond of June, her mild manner and Southern style and charm seemed an easy target for of- fice punsters; however, this high school debater could launch a level- ing rebuttal that clearly showed she was no Grannie Grammar; in- deed, her wonderful wit and pleasing humor coupled with sincere concern and compassion made many lengthy legislative days easier to endure; moreover, her engaging enthusiasm showed younger con- temporaries that age is truly only a state of mind; and WHEREAS, as she begins a new section of her life, we wish June Weaver frequent and fulfilling visits with her three children and two extraordinary grandchildren, all the marvelous travel experiences that she has envisioned, reading for pleasure rather than punctuation, kind bridge cards, and maximum years filled with life’s best joys, pleasures, and gifts; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That with sincere admiration and appreciation, Mrs. June Weaver is thanked for laudable service to the Legislature of Alabama. These sentiments are conveyed by copy of this resolution, accompanied by our genuine hope that her future will include the ultimate blessings of good health and happiness. COMMENDING TAIWAN ON ITS DEMOCRACY AND ITS CONTRIBUTIONS TO PROMOTE WORLD PEACE, FREEDOM, AND HUMAN RIGHTS; SUPPORTING TAIWAN’S REGULAR SESSION 431 10th Day - March 4, 2004 EFFORTS TO JOIN THE UNITED NATIONS, WORLD HEALTH ORGANIZATION AND OTHER INTERNATIONAL ORGANI- ZATIONS; AND RECOGNIZING THE 2004 PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION IN TAIWAN. WHEREAS, Taiwan and the United States of America are friends and allies of long standing, both dearly cherishing the com- monly shared values of freedom, democracy, and human rights; and WHEREAS, Taiwan has the world’s 16th largest economy; it is the 8th largest trading partner of the United States as well as the 5th largest market for US agricultural products; and WHEREAS, the State of Alabama and Taiwan have enjoyed mutually beneficial sister-state relations since 1983 with the prospect of further growth; and WHEREAS, Taiwan is a willing and contributing member of the world community, distinguishing itself in the areas of education, economy, and democratization; and WHEREAS, the State of Alabama looks forward to facilitat- ing and enhancing trade and investment opportunities with Taiwan; and WHEREAS, the upcoming presidential election in Taiwan demonstrates to the free world that democracy flourishes in Taiwan; indeed, the Taiwan citizens can freely express their will and deter- mine their own future without coercion, such as the hostile missile deployment from Mainland China; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That we join Alabama citizens in extending best wishes and support to the people of Taiwan; that we support Taiwan’s efforts to join the United Na- tions, the World Health Organization, and other international organi- zations; and that we recognize and support the 2004 Presidential Election in Taiwan. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That a copy of this resolu- tion be forwarded to Director General Rong-Chuan Wu of the Taipei Economic and Cultural Office in Atlanta, Georgia. COMMENDING ANTOINE PETTWAY ON HIS OUTSTANDING ATHLETIC ACCOMPLISHMENTS. WHEREAS, it is with highest commendation that we note the outstanding athletic accomplishments of Antoine Pettway, the talent- ed Alabama Crimson Tide Basketball player; and WHEREAS, a six-foot guard from Alberta, Antoine Pettway is a fearless player who meets any challenge on the court; offered a scholarship to Jacksonville State, his heart was at The University of Alabama so he worked hard to prove himself as a walk-on; and WHEREAS, as a freshman, Antoine Pettway played in 29 games, earning an athletic scholarship in July 2001; as a sophomore, he played in 35 games and in addition to the red shoes he wore that year, he is probably most remembered for his layup as time expired against Florida that season, giving Alabama a 65-64 victory and wrapping up a share of the SEC regular season championship; and WHEREAS, in his junior year, Antoine Pettway played in 29 games and started in 10; and as a senior, he has started in all 26 games and is averaging 9.0 points, 3.4 assists, and 3.5 rebounds per game, the best in his career; and WHEREAS, Antoine Pettway personifies that positive ability to persevere and win, and his actions embody the spirit of The Uni- versity of Alabama Crimson Tide, thus bringing pride and honor to all the citizens of the great State of Alabama; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That we hereby acknowledge and applaud the many athletic accomplishments of Antoine Pettway and convey to him our highest praise and sincere good wishes by providing a copy of this resolution for appropriate presentation. HONORING JOHN AND CHRISTY BOLLE FOR SERVING IN THE UNITED STATES AIR FORCE FOR 17 AND 15 YEARS RESPECTIVELY. WHEREAS, it is with honor and pride that highest commen- dation and honor is extended to John and Christy Bolle for serving in the United States Air Force for 17 and 15 years respectively; and WHEREAS, John and Christy Bolle have just returned from a four and one-half years assignment at Ramstein Air Base in Germa- ny where they were supporting numerous operations in support of the war on terrorism; and WHEREAS, John Bolle was deployed in support of the Kos- ovo Air Campaign within 48 hours’ notice and was responsible for ensuring personnel accountability for deployed commanders; he was assigned to Headquarters United States Air Forces in Europe, Direc- torate of Personnel, where he was deployed in support of Operation ALLIED FORCE and worked with the Birmingham Air National Guard unit during the Kosovo Air Campaign; he also served during the first Gulf War where he monitored and managed personnel throughout the theater of operations ensuring proper use of military assets; and WHEREAS, Christy Bolle was deployed to Northern Iraq, opening Bashir Air Field, setting up the northern front for American forces during the opening hours of Operation IRAQI FREEDOM and ensuring delivery capabilities for troops, food, and equipment; she has served in numerous locations throughout Europe, Africa, and the 528 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2004 12th Day - March 11, 2004 Middle East as an Airfield Manager and surveyor validating airfield suitability and capabilities; and WHEREAS, John and Christy, the son-in-law and daughter of Lieutenant Colonel (Retired) Jack Buckner and Ginger Avery, have received numerous awards and decorations for defending the United States Constitution/Freedom; indeed, they have earned the deepest admiration and utmost respect of all Alabamians and Americans for their sacrifice to protect freedom and liberty at home and abroad; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That John and Christy Bolle are hereby recognized and praised for serving their country with valor and it is directed that a copy of this resolution shall be presented with highest tribute and admiration. COMMENDING MARY BAKER EDDY POSTHU- MOUSLY FOR HER OUTSTANDING ACHIEVEMENTS DUR- ING NATIONAL WOMEN’S HISTORY MONTH IN MARCH 2004. WHEREAS, we note with highest commendation and esteem 620 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2004 15th Day - March 30, 2004 the outstanding achievements of Mary Baker Eddy during National Women’s History Month in March 2004; and WHEREAS, in 1821, near Concord, New Hampshire, Mary Morse Baker was born to a family of devoted Congregationalists; and WHEREAS, at the time of the First Women’s Rights Conven- tion in 1848, Mary Morse Baker’s life was extremely difficult as a chronically ill, widowed, single mother with no property to call her own; despite these challenges, Mary Baker Eddy never gave up and at the time of her death in 1910, her accomplishments were numer- ous; and WHEREAS, Mary Baker Eddy founded the Church of Christ, Scientist, which today has some 2,200 congregations in 70 countries; in 1898, she founded the Christian Science Publishing Society and in 1908, she launched The Christian Science Monitor, an international daily newspaper that has won seven Pulitzer Prizes; she truly was a pioneer in the field of mind/body medicine, a healer, and teacher; COMMENDING THE ALABAMA DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC HEALTH FOR ITS EFFORTS TO FIGHT CANCER 622 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2004 15th Day - March 30, 2004 AND URGING THE DEPARTMENT TO FOCUS MORE SPECIF- ICALLY ON CERVICAL CANCER. WHEREAS, the Alabama Department of Public Health and other public and private organizations have partnered to form the Al- abama Comprehensive Cancer Control Coalition to develop an inte- grated and coordinated approach to reduce the incidence, morbidity, and mortality of cancer through prevention, early detection, treat- ment, rehabilitation, and palliation; and WHEREAS, the knowledge and technology exist today to significantly reduce the incidence and mortality from cancer; and WHEREAS, the American Cancer Society estimates that in the United States, 10,520 new cases of invasive cervical cancer will be diagnosed in 2004, and 3,900 women will die of the disease; and WHEREAS, approximately half of the women who are diag- nosed with cervical cancer are between the ages of 35 and 55 years, with the median age of 47 years, the youngest median age for all fe- male reproductive cancers; and WHEREAS, human Papillomavirus (HPV) has been detected in up to 99.7 percent of cervical cancers; and WHEREAS, although HPV is the most common sexually transmitted viral disease in the world 70 percent of Americans have never heard of it; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That we hereby recognize the importance of the work of the Alabama Depart- ment of Public Health and Comprehensive Cancer Control Coalition to identify the causes and the means of controlling cancer; that we commend them for their efforts on behalf of the citizens of Alabama, and that we support their work. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That we urge the Alabama Department of Public Health and the Comprehensive Cancer Control Coalition to review the statistical and qualitative data on the preva- lence and burden of cervical cancer; to raise public awareness on the causes and nature of cervical cancer, personal risk factors, and value of prevention; to identify strategies and new technologies including newly introduced vaccines which are effective in preventing and con- trolling the risk of cervical cancer; to include such information and strategies relating to cervical cancer in the statewide Comprehensive Cancer Control Plan; and to report annually on the status of cervical REGULAR SESSION 623 15th Day - March 30, 2004 cancer intervention activities throughout the state through the depart- ment’s annual report submitted to members of the Legislature. The Senate proceeded to further consideration of the Resolu- tion, SJR64. The question was on the House amendment. On motion of Senator Bedford, the Senate concurred in and adopted the following House amendment to the Resolution, SJR64, to wit: SUBSTITUTE FOR SJR64 SJR64 AFFIRMING THAT THE U.S. ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY SHOULD ADOPT RULES ON MER- CURY EMISSION CONTROL THAT ARE BASED ON A CAP AND TRADE SYSTEM AND URGING THE AGENCY TO EN- SURE THAT THE RULES FAIRLY DISTRIBUTE THE RESPON- SIBILITY FOR MERCURY EMISSION CONTROL AMONG ALL RANKS OF COAL. WHEREAS, the State of Alabama contains vast bituminous coal reserves that are important to the economic welfare and employ- ment of its citizens and vital to our nation’s energy security; and REGULAR SESSION 1605 23rd Day - April 21, 2004 WHEREAS, the State of Alabama believes the production of plentiful and affordable energy derived from coal is fundamental to its future growth; and WHEREAS, the State of Alabama supports the production and use of these coal resources in an environmentally sound manner and in a manner assuring good health and safety to coal miners and to all Americans; and WHEREAS, all Americans are deserving of and expect clean air and water; and WHEREAS, the Legislature of the State of Alabama specifi- cally supports fair, reasonable, and sound federal regulations to fairly address the control of emissions from coal-fired electric utilities; and WHEREAS, the proposed mercury emission control rules published by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) in the January 30, 2004, Federal Register propose that the Agency adopt ei- ther a cap and trade approach or a Maximum Achievable Control Technology or MACT approach; and WHEREAS, certain aspects of the MACT approach impose a difficult or, in some instances, impossible burden on Alabama’s bitu- minous coal industry, while imposing little or no burden on subbitu- minous coal industries from western states; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That the Legislature of the State of Alabama, by majority consensus, hereby affirms the position that the (EPA), in its final mercury emission con- trol rules should adopt the cap and trade approach so that there will not be a severe negative impact on the state’s bituminous coal indus- try and on the state’s electric customers. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That we hereby urge the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency to adopt a cap and trade ap- proach that fairly distributes the responsibility for mercury emission reductions among all ranks of coal, and that a copy of this resolution be provided to the Director of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, the Governor of Alabama, the Director of the Alabama De- partment of Environmental Management, and to the members of Al- abama’s Congressional Delegation.

COMMENDING SOUTHERN RURAL HOME HEALTH CARE FOR RECEIVING A 2004 EXCELLENCE IN HEALTHCARE QUALITY AWARD. WHEREAS, highest commendation is herein extended to the Southern Rural Home Health Care Center and its staff for receiving a 2004 Excellence in Healthcare Quality Award sponsored by the Al- abama Quality Assurance Foundation, a nonprofit organization who serves approximately 700,000 Medicare beneficiaries and 6,000 pro- viders throughout the state; and WHEREAS, Southern Rural Home Health Care was recog- nized as one of the state’s leading health care facilities for its out- standing work with patients who suffer from urinary incontinence; and WHEREAS, delivering high quality and innovative health- care, the Southern Rural Home Health Care has created a comprehen- sive Plan of Action to improve urinary incontinence in men, women, and children in every social and economic level; and WHEREAS, indeed, the staff of Southern Rural Home Health Care not only provides service, comfort, and assistance to its patients, but also is deeply committed to their responsibilities, while providing a unique tradition of exceptional medical care; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That highest commendation and congratulations are herein extended to Southern Rural Home Health Care and its staff for receiving the prestigious 2004 Excellence in Healthcare Quality Awards sponsored by the Al- abama Quality Assurance Foundation and it is directed that a copy of this resolution be provided for appropriate display with sincere best wishes for all future endeavors. Senator Bedford requested and received unanimous consent to suspend the provisions of Senate Rule 55 and the Resolution was adopted by the Senate.

COMMENDING THE DUAL-PARTY RELAY REGULAR SESSION 907 17th Day - April 6, 2004 FUND ADMINISTRATOR COMMITTEE FOR OUTSTANDING SERVICE IN CONNECTION WITH THE ALABAMA DUAL- PARTY RELAY SYSTEM AND A READING SERVICE FOR SIGHT-IMPAIRED PERSONS TO THE CITIZENS OF ALA- BAMA. WHEREAS, the Alabama Dual-Party Relay System (System) was established by Section 37-1-80.2, Code of Alabama 1975, which provides that the Alabama Public Service Commission (PSC) shall impose a surcharge on each access line of each customer of local ex- change companies operating in Alabama to fund a dual-party relay system, whereby a deaf or hearing-impaired person may communi- cate with other such persons or with normal hearing persons via tele- phone; and WHEREAS, Section 37-1-80.2 provides that the funds shall be collected and deposited to a private fund to be kept separate from all other funds and used solely for the administration of the relay sys- tem; and WHEREAS, the PSC appointed the Dual-Party Relay System Fund Administrator Committee (Committee), by PSC Resolution dated June 10, 1988, which has successfully implemented and admin- istered the System; and WHEREAS, the Committee also established a reading ser- vice for sight-impaired persons, with the encouragement of the Ala- bama Senate, by Resolution dated April 17, 2002; and WHEREAS, the Committee, in consultation with its auditor, has determined that it is necessary, in the interest of efficiency and necessity, to employ a private sector administrator for the private funds administered by the System; and WHEREAS, the Committee has done an admirable job ad- ministering the System in serving the needs of all Alabamians; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That we hereby acknowledge and applaud the efforts of the Committee in ad- ministering the System in Alabama and ratify its efforts in privately contracting with an administrator to assist in its tasks and direct that a copy of this resolution be sent to the Committee. COMMENDING JULIE MCINNIS FOR OUT- STANDING PROFESSIONAL ACHIEVEMENTS. WHEREAS, in an effort to acknowledge and commend Ala- bamians of notable accomplishments, it is a pleasure to honor and 1298 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2004 21st Day - April 15, 2004 congratulate Julie McInnis, Director of Membership Services for the Alabama Association of School Boards, who has provided her ser- vice, ability, and tireless devotion to the public school boards and stu- dents of Alabama for nearly 20 years; and WHEREAS, through her exemplary efforts, Ms. McInnis has made a positive impact as an advocate for Alabama’s public school children through the Alabama Association of School Boards, where she has ably served in numerous roles, including Staff Assistant, Di- rector of Communication, Director of Special Projects, and for the past eight years as Director of Membership Services; and WHEREAS, Ms. McInnis has devoted considerable time and unparalleled professional leadership in furthering public education; of special note is her work in coordinating the association’s School Board Member Academy, where her innovative and creative efforts, as well as her admirable work ethic, have enriched the understanding and knowledge of innumberable school board members; worthy ef- forts resulting in better administered school systems throughout our state; and WHEREAS, Ms. McInnis has developed strong relationships with state Legislators and has unrelentingly labored on behalf of Al- abama’s school students; indeed she was a trusted source for informa- tion in making key education policy decisions and her abilities and skills were respected and appreciated by the entire legislative and ed- ucational community; and WHEREAS, Ms. Julie McInnis will retire from the Alabama Association of School Boards on June 1, 2004, after nearly two de- cades of service; and it is most appropriate to recognize the contribu- tions of this gracious lady to the State of Alabama; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That with high admiration and sincere appreciation, we commend Ms. Julie McInnis for her distinguished service as Director of Membership Ser- vices for the Alabama Association of School Boards and her multiple contributions to public education. A copy of this resolution of sincere regard and esteem shall be provided along with our best wishes in all future endeavors. RECOGNIZING THE 10TH ANNIVERSARY OF THE ALABAMA BOATING SAFETY REFORM ACT OF 1994. WHEREAS, April 28, 2004, marks the 10th anniversary of the approval of the Alabama Boating Safety Reform Act of 1994; leg- islation which has had a profound and positive impact on the citizens of Alabama; and WHEREAS, Act 94-652 of the 1994 Regular Session, among other worthy features, included penalties relating to the operation of a vessel or marine device under the influence of alcohol or controlled substances; provided for the power of arrest at the scene of a boating accident; provided for the crime of homicide by vessel; regulated the use of personal watercrafts; required the use of personal flotation de- vices; and provided for boater safety certification; and WHEREAS, the 1994 act better ensures the safety and en- hances the recreational pleasures of Alabamians who increasingly en- joy the beautiful waterways of our state; and WHEREAS, the act, also known as the Roberson-Archer Act, has proven exceptionally effective and beneficial; in the first year of application boating fatalities decreased a remarkable 50 percent and 1358 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2004 21st Day - April 15, 2004 the accident and fatality rates continue to remain impressively low; and WHEREAS, the most significant aspect of the reform statute was the establishment of a mandatory operator licensing program, an innovative plan that has proven unquestionably worthwhile, as evi- denced by the fact it has become a model program emulated by many states throughout our nation; and WHEREAS, on the 10th anniversary of this innovative law, it is appropriate to highlight this legislative success story and remind the public of its continuing value and important benefits; now there- fore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That the 10th anniversary of the Alabama Boating Safety Reform Act of 1994 is recognized; and former Commissioner of the Department of Conser- vation and Natural Resources Charles Grimsley, Mr. Mike Bolton of the Birmingham News, members of this legislative body, and other participating parties are proudly congratulated for this legislation which has had a tangible, immediate, and positive impact in protect- ing the health, welfare, and recreational pursuits of the citizens of Al- abama. REQUESTING U.S. GOVERNMENTAL OFFI- CIALS TO SUPPORT ACCESSIBILITY AND COMMUNICA- TION ISSUES CONCERNING DEAF AND HARD OF HEARING CITIZENS. WHEREAS, the Americans With Disabilities Act of 1990 was intended to ensure accessibility to the mainstream of life for all persons with disabilities, including all aspects of public communica- tion for people who are deaf or hard of hearing; however, 14 years af- ter enactment of the law, widespread adoption of captioning stan- dards in all audible media and the nation’s public facilities has yet to reach acceptable standards; and WHEREAS, the absence of captioning in various areas such as emergency notification systems, movie theaters, airport visuals and in-flight movies, train and transit communication, television pro- gramming, and more are still evident; and WHEREAS, at a time when there is an increasing need for ex- panded captioning services that address the accessibility issues put forth in the Americans With Disabilities Act, recent actions by the U.S. Department of Education have resulted in censorship of televi- sion programs selected for captioning, as recommended by a deaf consumer advisory board and to be financed with allocated federal funds; and WHEREAS, the Alabama Legislature proudly recognizes the contributions and accomplishments of people who are deaf in the State of Alabama and acknowledges the significant rights of all per- sons with disabilities to equal accessibility to public communication and facilities; and WHEREAS, this legislative body thinks it is proper to request 1362 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2004 21st Day - April 15, 2004 U.S. Government officials to take appropriate action to better ensure that the rights of deaf and hard of hearing citizens are considered and protected; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That we are in full support of ideals advanced by the Alabama Association of the Deaf, which advocates for appropriate accessibility in public commu- nication, and we request the U.S. Department of Education to guard against censorship of captioned programming to the greatest extent possible. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That we respectfully request that President George Bush and the Alabama U.S. Congressional Delegation provide leadership and support for expanded accessibility in public facilities and for communication issues concerning the 28 million Americans who are deaf or hard of hearing. A copy of this resolution shall be provided to the Secretary of the U.S. Department of Education, the President of the United States, and each member of the Alabama U.S. Congressional Delegation so that our concerns re- garding this important matter are known. HONORING MRS. ELIZABETH HOBBIE SMITH ON THE OCCASION OF HER 80TH BIRTHDAY. WHEREAS, Mrs. Elizabeth Hobbie Smith will mark a mile- stone in her life on April 24, 2004, her 80th birthday, and upon this auspicious occasion, she is deserving of special recognition and heartiest congratulations; and WHEREAS, Mrs. Smith, a native of Montgomery County, is a graduate of Lanier High School, attended Huntingdon College, and is the dearly loved and respected mother of Henry Hobbie Wright; and WHEREAS, she was appointed by former Mayor Earl James as Director of the Urban Renewal Program in Montgomery, Ala- bama, and by former President Jimmy Carter as Director of the Farm- ers Home Administration for the State of Alabama from 1977 to 1981; since 1992, Mrs. Smith has served with distinction as Assistant to the President of Faulkner University and as an esteemed member of the Faulkner University Board of Trustees since April 19, 1970; and REGULAR SESSION 1561 22nd Day - April 20, 2004 WHEREAS, Mrs. Smith is especially thanked and applauded for her very generous support and donations to Faulkner University, as well as numerous other charitable causes, and is an inspiration and blessing to her family and friends, whose lives are infinitely better for having been touched by her care and concern for their happiness and well-being; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That Mrs. Elizabeth Hobbie Smith is congratulated on the momentous occasion of her 80th birthday, April 24, 2004, and it is directed that she receive a copy of this resolution that she may know of our best wishes for a special lady who has been so richly blessed by God. Senator Mitchell requested and received unanimous consent to suspend the provisions of Senate Rule 55 and the Resolution was adopted by the Senate.

MOURNING THE DEATH OF MRS. JULIA COMPTON MOORE. WHEREAS, the Alabama Legislature notes with deep sad- ness and regret the death of Mrs. Julia “Julie” Compton Moore on April 18, 2004, at the age of 75 years; and WHEREAS, born February 10, 1929, to Army Colonel Louis J. Compton and Elizabeth Boon Compton in Fort Sill, Oklahoma, Julia Moore was a graduate of Chevy Chase Junior College in Chevy Chase, Maryland, and attended the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill; and WHEREAS, in 1949, Julia married Hal Moore who later commanded the First Battalion, 7th Cavalry in the Battle of the Ia Drang Valley in Vietnam in 1965; the impact of this battle at home in Columbus, Georgia, was depicted in the 2002 Paramount release, “We Were Soldiers”; and WHEREAS, Mrs. Moore challenged and stopped the U. S. Army’s impersonal practice of delivering notices of combat death by taxi and the Army instituted the practice of delivering compassionate notices through uniformed personnel, now a standard procedure; she also supported the day care centers and wives clubs in order to take better care of the enlisted soldier and his family and she was instru- mental in starting the Army Community Service organizations; and WHEREAS, Mrs. Moore was a member of Pi Phi Sorority and an integral part of the community, serving as a Brownie and Girl Scout Leader, Cub Scout Den Mother, and Red Cross volunteer in the Army hospitals; and WHEREAS, left to cherish the memory of Mrs. Julia Moore are her devoted husband of 55 years, Lieutenant General (Retired) Harold G. Moore; children, Greg (Evelyn) Moore, Lieutenant Colo- nel (Retired) Steve (Donna) Moore, Julie Moore Thompson, Cecile Moore (Terry) Rainey, and Lieutenant Colonel David (Theresa) Moore; and 12 grandchildren; and WHEREAS, the death of Mrs. Julia Moore has indeed left a deep void in the life of her community and in the hearts of her family, neighbors, and friends who knew and loved her as a warm and gra- 1586 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2004 23rd Day - April 21, 2004 cious lady who cared and showed concern for the happiness and well- being of others; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That even as we mourn her death, we give thanks for the blessing of Mrs. Julia Compton Moore’s life and extend deepest sympathy to her husband, whose grief we share, and for whom a copy of this resolution shall be provided. On motion of Senator Bedford, the Senate concurred in and adopted the following House amendment to the Resolution, SJR64, to wit: SUBSTITUTE FOR SJR64 SJR64 AFFIRMING THAT THE U.S. ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY SHOULD ADOPT RULES ON MER- CURY EMISSION CONTROL THAT ARE BASED ON A CAP AND TRADE SYSTEM AND URGING THE AGENCY TO EN- SURE THAT THE RULES FAIRLY DISTRIBUTE THE RESPON- SIBILITY FOR MERCURY EMISSION CONTROL AMONG ALL RANKS OF COAL. WHEREAS, the State of Alabama contains vast bituminous coal reserves that are important to the economic welfare and employ- ment of its citizens and vital to our nation’s energy security; and REGULAR SESSION 1605 23rd Day - April 21, 2004 WHEREAS, the State of Alabama believes the production of plentiful and affordable energy derived from coal is fundamental to its future growth; and WHEREAS, the State of Alabama supports the production and use of these coal resources in an environmentally sound manner and in a manner assuring good health and safety to coal miners and to all Americans; and WHEREAS, all Americans are deserving of and expect clean air and water; and WHEREAS, the Legislature of the State of Alabama specifi- cally supports fair, reasonable, and sound federal regulations to fairly address the control of emissions from coal-fired electric utilities; and WHEREAS, the proposed mercury emission control rules published by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) in the January 30, 2004, Federal Register propose that the Agency adopt ei- ther a cap and trade approach or a Maximum Achievable Control Technology or MACT approach; and WHEREAS, certain aspects of the MACT approach impose a difficult or, in some instances, impossible burden on Alabama’s bitu- minous coal industry, while imposing little or no burden on subbitu- minous coal industries from western states; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That the Legislature of the State of Alabama, by majority consensus, hereby affirms the position that the (EPA), in its final mercury emission con- trol rules should adopt the cap and trade approach so that there will not be a severe negative impact on the state’s bituminous coal indus- try and on the state’s electric customers. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That we hereby urge the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency to adopt a cap and trade ap- proach that fairly distributes the responsibility for mercury emission reductions among all ranks of coal, and that a copy of this resolution be provided to the Director of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, the Governor of Alabama, the Director of the Alabama De- partment of Environmental Management, and to the members of Al- abama’s Congressional Delegation.

ENCOURAGING ALL COLLEGE AGE STU- DENTS TO BE VACCINATED AGAINST HEPATITIS B. WHEREAS, around 5,000 individuals die from Hepatitis B infection every year in the United States; and WHEREAS, Hepatitis B is a viral disease that attacks the liv- er and can cause jaundice, permanent liver damage, and even death; and, after smoking, Hepatitis B is the world’s leading known cause of cancer; and WHEREAS, Hepatitis B is spread through blood and other body fluids, including sweat, tears, and other bodily secretions, and can survive for at least one month on contaminated surfaces in some circumstances; moreover, Hepatitis B is up to 100 times more conta- gious than the virus that causes AIDS; and WHEREAS, according to the Centers For Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), there are 78,000 new Hepatitis B infections each year despite the availability of a safe vaccine; further, the cost to treat the estimated 1 to 1.25 million people in the United States with chronic Hepatitis B exceeds $700 million; and WHEREAS, according to the CDC, the highest rate of disease occurs in persons 20-49 years old, and intercollegiate student ath- letes, intramural sports participants, and athletic club team members are especially at risk because of possible contact with the blood or body fluids of an infected player through routine scrapes and cuts re- ceived during the course of the game; and WHEREAS, contact with a contaminated needle used in tat- tooing, ear or body piercing, or intravenous drug use and sexual con- tact with an infected partner are frequent sources of infection; and WHEREAS, a national study published in the October 1995 issue of the Journal of American Medical Association shows that Hepatitis B vaccine saves lives and is cost-effective by preventing costly liver disease and liver transplants; the cost per death prevented is $94,724; and WHEREAS, the Hepatitis B vaccine is a highly safe and ef- fective vaccine for the prevention of Hepatitis B disease and there is no scientific evidence that the vaccine causes multiple sclerosis, au- tism, or any other neurological disease; indeed, promoting vaccina- tion to prevent this deadly disease is most appropriate and desirable; now therefore, 1928 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2004 27th Day - May 4, 2004 BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That all col- lege age students are encouraged to receive a vaccination for Hepati- tis B. A copy of this resolution shall be provided to the State Health Officer, so that these important sentiments may be fully conveyed. Senator Figures requested and received unanimous consent to suspend the provisions of Senate Rule 55 and the Resolution was adopted by the Senate.

HONORING THE LIFE OF FORMER ALABAMA HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES AND SENATE MEMBER, ED- WARD “BIG ED” D. ROBERTSON. WHEREAS, it is with highest commendation that we honor the life of former Alabama House of Representatives and Senate Member, Edward “Big Ed” D. Robertson; and WHEREAS, born in 1930, Edward Robertson grew up in the Piney Woods community in North Tuscaloosa County near New Lexington and moved to Northport in 1951; and 1948 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2004 27th Day - May 4, 2004 WHEREAS, elected to the Northport City Council in 1964, Edward Robertson served for three years and was elected to fill the unexpired term of Alabama House of Representatives Member, Hugh Thomas; after serving for 11 years, he served a term in the Alabama Senate in 1979, and was elected Mayor of Northport in 1984; and WHEREAS, the campaign slogan of Edward Robertson was “Solid as a Rock” and over the years he distributed thousands of small rocks with his name, the slogan, and a flower painted on them; and WHEREAS, Mr. Robertson retired from Uniroyal Goodrich in 1985 after working nearly 36 years at the plant; and WHEREAS, Edward was married to his devoted wife of 53 years, Jean, who assisted him in his duties at the State Capitol and with the constituents; they were blessed with a daughter, Donna; son- in-law, Julian; and two grandsons; and WHEREAS, a bold politician who stood for what he thought was right, Edward Robertson truly fought for the good of the com- mon man; he indeed earned the respect and admiration of those with whom he was associated during his successful and rewarding career; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That we hereby recognize the life of former Alabama House of Representa- tives and Senate Member, Edward “Big Ed” D. Robertson and do fur- ther direct that a copy of this resolution be provided for appropriate presentation. COMMENDING THE CITY OF HOOVER PUB- LIC SAFETY CENTER REFUELING FACILITY. WHEREAS, increased ozone levels in Jefferson and Shelby Counties have been detrimental to public health, the environment, and economic development in the area; and WHEREAS, harmful emissions from cars and trucks cause increased health risks due to higher ozone levels; however, the usage of E85 fuel (consisting of 85% ethanol and 15% gasoline) can reduce emissions that lead to ozone formation; and WHEREAS, flexible fuel vehicles can run on E85 and gaso- line, a renewable fuel which is primarily produced domestically from agricultural products; and WHEREAS, job development and domestic energy security can be positively impacted by the increased use of E85 and centers distributing the fuel; the city of Hoover Public Safety Center Refuel- ing Facility, which recently opened, will distribute environmentally friendly E85 fuel to its fleet of FFV’s and to other public agency fleets in the area; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That the re- duction of ozone levels should be a top priority not only in Jefferson and Shelby Counties, but throughout the state of Alabama, and it is directed that a copy of this resolution be provided for appropriate dis- play at the city of Hoover Public Safety Center Refueling Facility. WHEREAS, the Alabama Legislature notes with deep grati- tude the incalculable contributions of the members of the United States Armed Forces in making our military service the powerful force it is today and our nation a shrine of democracy, the ultimate blessing earned by the remarkable courage, perseverance, and devo- tion of our veterans; and WHEREAS, the contributions and sacrifices of Cleburne County veterans are honored by a local War Memorial administered by American Legion Post 19, in Heflin, Alabama; and WHEREAS, American Legion Post 19 wishes to have appro- priate signs placed on Highway 9 and in the City of Heflin directing motorists to the local War Memorial, so that well-earned respect and appreciation may be given to our veterans; and WHEREAS, such action is proper and appropriate, and we wish to express our support concerning this effort; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That in trib- ute to the men and women of the United States Armed Forces, we re- quest the Department of Transportation and the City of Heflin, in consultation with American Legion Post 19, to place appropriate signs on Highway 9 and in the City of Heflin indicating directions to the War Memorial in Heflin, Alabama. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That a copy of this resolu- tion be provided to the Department of Transportation, the City of Heflin, and American Legion Post 19, so that each may know of our admiration and approval of this effort to further honor veterans of Cleburne County. to provide employee protective provisions with respect to the operation of public transportation ser- vice by the Authority; to provide provisions to protect employees of any existing transportation system acquired by the Authority; to pre- 2206 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2004 29th Day - May 6, 2004 vent the incorporation of any subsequent authority by the Authoriz- ing County; to provide for the effective date of the Act; to repeal Act No. 87-449 of the 1987 Regular Session.

To provide that any tenant or tenants who received sewer service shall be solely responsible for the sewer bill. GREG PAPPAS, Clerk. HOUSE MESSAGE On motion of Senator Biddle, the Senate concurred in and adopted the following House amendment to the Bill, SB357, the title of which is set out in the foregoing Message from the House, to wit: SUBSTITUTE FOR SB357 A BILL TO BE ENTITLED AN ACT To provide that any tenant or tenants who received water and sewer service shall be solely responsible for the water and sewer bill. Section 1. Notwithstanding any other provision of law, any bill for water and sewer service received in the name of a tenant or tenants, shall be the sole responsibility of the tenant or tenants and shall not constitute a lien on the property where the water and sewer service was received. Section 2. All laws or parts of laws which conflict with this act are repealed. Section 3. This act shall become effective on the first day of the third month following its passage and approval by the Governor, or its otherwise becoming law. CREATING A JOINT LEGISLATIVE COMMIT- TEE FOR THE ALABAMA CHAMBER AUTOMATION SYS- TEM WHEREAS, the Alabama Legislature is presently in need to upgrade the Alabama Chamber Automation System (ACAS) for use by the members of the Alabama Legislature beginning with the Reg- ular Session of 2005, and, 2374 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2004 30th Day - May 17, 2004 WHEREAS, there is a need for policies and procedures to be formalized prior to the upgrade of ACAS at the beginning of the Reg- ular Session of 2005; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That there is hereby created a joint interim legislative committee for the Alabama Chamber Automation System (ACAS). The committee shall be com- posed of three (3) members of the Senate appointed by the Lt. Gov- ernor and the President Pro Tempore; three (3) members of the House of Representatives appointed by the Speaker; the Clerk of the House of Representatives or his designee; and the Secretary of the Senate or his designee. The chair and vice chair of the committee shall be elect- ed at the first meeting of the committee; the committee shall formal- ize policies and procedures for the use of laptop computers by the membership of the Alabama Legislature. The committee shall advise the Clerk of the House and the Secretary of the Senate with regard to the information enhancements needed on the ACAS system. The leg- islative members of the ACAS Joint Interim Legislative Committee shall serve as the pilot project testees when the upgrade is ready for testing prior to the 2005 Regular Session. Upon the request of the chair, the Secretary of the Senate and the Clerk of the House shall provide the clerical assistance necessary for the committee’s work. Each member of the committee shall be en- titled to his or her regular legislative compensation, his or her per di- em, and travel expenses for each day he or she attends a meeting of the committee which shall be paid out of any funds appropriated to the use of the Legislature, upon warrants drawn on the State Comp- troller upon requisitions signed by the chair of the committee. Not- withstanding the foregoing, no member shall receive additional leg- islative compensation or per diem when the Legislature is in session or if a member is being paid any other payments on the same dates for attendance of other state business. The committee shall stand dis- solved and discharged of any further duties and liabilities at the end of the Regular Session of 2006. The total expenditure of the commit- tee shall not exceed five thousand dollars ($5,000.00). RECOGNIZING THE 50TH ANNIVERSARY OF BROWN V. BOARD OF EDUCATION AND ENCOURAGING FURTHER COMMITMENT TO ITS PRINCIPLES AND PURPOS- ES. REGULAR SESSION 2399 30th Day - May 17, 2004 WHEREAS, today, May 17, 2004, marks the 50th Anniversa- ry of the landmark U.S. Supreme Court case of Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka, Kansas, which held unconstitutional the previ- ously existing “separate but equal” doctrine of racially segregated schools in this country; and WHEREAS, many credit this decision as sparking the civil rights movement and leading to the enactment of federal and state laws that ended official discrimination and segregation; indeed, the legacy of this opinion was the reaffirmation of the principles of the 14th Amendment to the Constitution of the United States regarding the rights of all Americans to equal protection of the law; and WHEREAS, significant progress has been made in the years since 1954, and today, more than ever, Alabamians judge each other not by the color of their skins but by the content of their character; yet, as in most endeavors, there is room for additional improvement and advancement concerning this most fundamental freedom; and WHEREAS, it is fortunate that, on this most significant anni- versary date, we may acknowledge the importance of this case and its impact on our nation and state, and that we may encourage govern- mental and educational leaders to further dedicate and devote their energies and resources to achieving the preeminent precepts therein contained; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That we, in concert and conjunction with the Legislative Black Caucus, recog- nize the historic and cultural significance of the 50th Anniversary of the landmark decision of Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka, Kansas. President George Bush, Governor Bob Riley, governmental officials, and state educational officials are respectfully requested to strive on a daily basis to completely fulfill the just and right principle of equality for all as advocated and advanced by this judicial decision in order that no child or adult will be left behind. A copy of this res- olution shall be provided to President Bush, Governor Riley, the State Board of Education, state and local superintendents of education, and members of state boards of trustees, so that these officials may know of and share these sentiments with other governmental and educa- tional officials. said committee substitute being as follows: A BILL TO BE ENTITLED AN ACT Prohibiting a state department or agency from placing or otherwise revealing the Social Security number of a person on any document available for public inspection without the express consent of the person with certain exceptions. BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALABAMA: Section 1. Notwithstanding any other law to the contrary, a state department or agency is prohibited from placing or otherwise revealing the Social Security number of a person on any document that is available for public inspection without the express consent of the person with the number, or the consent of that person's parent, custodian, legal guardian or legal representative. The foregoing prohibition shall not apply when a federal or state agency makes a request for or releases a Social Security number for a legitimate government purpose, or pursuant to a federal or state statute, regulation or federally funded program. Section 2. This act shall become effective on the first day of the third month following its passage and approval by the Governor, or its otherwise becoming law. SUBSTITUTE ADOPTED And the substitute was adopted.

RECOGNIZING TROY UNIVERSITY AS A UNI- FIED GLOBAL UNIVERSITY. WHEREAS, Troy University has globally served the citizens of Alabama and the United States with distinction and great merit for more than 118 years; and WHEREAS, with bold vision, the Board of Trustees and Ad- ministrative Leadership of Troy University, under the direction of Dr. Jack Hawkins, Jr., Chancellor of Troy University, has proceeded with a course of action to consolidate all campuses and sites into one Uni- versity on August 1, 2005; and WHEREAS, additionally, the University Leadership decided that unification of the system was necessary to achieve the following goals: Improve service to students by removing barriers to academic transfer; implement shared academic standards, policies and proce- dures at all Troy University campuses; and to promote a worldwide brand identity for Troy University; and WHEREAS, the unification will consolidate separate aca- demic accreditations of all the sites and campuses and unite more than 60 sites across 21 times zones in six continents into one affirma- tive academic accreditation; and FIRST EXTRAORDINARY SESSION 203 3rd Day - July 21, 2005 WHEREAS, the Alabama Senate commends the faculty and staff of Troy University for their tireless efforts in making this unifi- cation and transition possible; and WHEREAS, on July 29, 2005, Troy University will become a Unified Global University during an “Around the World in 60 Sites” celebration; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That it is with highest commendation that we recognize Troy University on this significant milestone on July 29, 2005, and, by copy of this reso- lution, on its commitment to excellence in providing quality educa- tion to the citizens of the great State of Alabama and around the world. Senator Mitchell requested and received unanimous consent to suspend the provisions of Senate Rule 55 and the Resolution was adopted by the Senate.

CONTINUING THE TAX CREDITS AUTHO- RIZED BY ARTICLE 9 OF CHAPTER 18, TITLE 40, CODE OF ALABAMA 1975. WHEREAS, in 2001, the Legislature passed the Alabama Income Tax Credit Act; and WHEREAS, Sections 40-18-240 to 40-18-250, inclusive, involve tax credits for investment companies that qualify to use them for projects at the Alabama Port Authority; and WHEREAS, a qualifying project under the statute is a project in which one or more investing companies that have a capital cost of at least eight million dollars ($8,000,000), and at which the predom- inant trade or business activity conducted will be industrial, ware- housing, or research; and WHEREAS, this legislation terminates on December 31, 2005; and WHEREAS, the Port Authority needs the credits to be extended an additional five years; and WHEREAS, the act authorizes extending the credits by a joint resolution; and WHEREAS, only two projects have qualified for the credits, yet many other projects could benefit by a credit extension; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That, pursu- ant to Section 40-18-249, Code of Alabama 1975, the capital credits available and authorized by Article 9 of Chapter 18, Title 40, Code of Alabama 1975, are continued from December 31, 2005, until Decem- ber 31, 2010. HONORING MARK’S OUTDOORS, CHOSEN BY FIELD AND STREAM MAGAZINE AS ONE OF THE TOP 10 HUNTING AND FISHING RETAIL OUTLETS IN THE UNITED STATES. WHEREAS, highest commendations are herein extended to Mark’s Outdoors upon being chosen by Field and Stream Magazine as one of the top 10 hunting and fishing retail outlets in the United States; and WHEREAS, Mark’s Outdoors, a 8,400-square-foot store in Vestavia Hills, is owned and operated by Mark Whitlock and de- scribed in Field and Stream Magazine as a “must see” for Alabama sportsmen; and WHEREAS, interesting data about Mark’s Outdoors include 7,900 days open; 636 years of employee experience in hunting and fishing; 23 employees; more than 13 million plastic worms sold; 17.5 million rounds of ammunition sold; and the fact that many children have been exposed to the life of hunting and fishing; and WHEREAS, this is indeed a prestigious honor to be featured in the August issue of Field and Stream Magazine and it is most fit- ting to commend Mark’s Outdoors for such a noteworthy recogni- tion; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That Mark’s Outdoors is highly commended upon being chosen by Field and Stream Magazine as one of the top 10 hunting and fishing retail out- lets in the United States and a copy of this resolution shall be provid- ed for appropriate presentation with our sincere best wishes for many more years of providing adventure in the outdoors. Senator Waggoner requested and received unanimous con- sent to suspend the provisions of Senate Rule 55 and the Resolution was adopted by the Senate.

MOURNING THE DEATH OF MR. HORACE DICK OF LINEVILLE, ALABAMA. WHEREAS, recorded with a sense of deep sorrow and loss is the death of Mr. Horace Dick of Lineville, Alabama, a longtime and beloved educator; and WHEREAS, Horace Dick served his country during World War II in the 802nd Field Artillery Unit, attached to General Patton; after the war, he started school in the Veterans Training Program and began teaching agriculture at Lineville High School; in the early 1960s until 1973, he served as principal and returned to the agriculture department, where he worked until 1980; and WHEREAS, through 58 years of their long and happy lives together, the commitment of Horace and Thea Dick not only enriched their lives but also the lives of their family and friends who witnessed their devotion to each other; and WHEREAS, Mr. Dick always showed his care and concern for the fortunate students who came under his tutelage and during his long career as a teacher and principal at Lineville High School, he earned the admiration and respect of all those with whom he was associated; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- 302 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2005 8th Day - February 24, 2005 BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That in sadness and regret the death of Mr. Horace Dick is hereby recorded, and sincerest sympathy is extended to his wife for whom a copy of this resolution shall be provided. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that a copy of this resolution also shall be presented to Lineville High School to be displayed in loving memory of Mr. Dick. Senator Dial requested and received unanimous consent to suspend the provisions of Senate Rule 55 and the Resolution was adopted by the Senate.
