DESIGNATING MARCH 4, 2005, AS MAC POR- TER DAY. WHEREAS, it is with highest commendation that we recog- nize March 4, 2005, as “Mac Porter Day” in honor of Dr. Charles McGavock Porter’s 34 years of service to the medical community; and WHEREAS, Dr. Porter is the founding physician of Mont- gomery Cardiovascular Associates, a thriving medical practice of more than 120 employees and physicians committed to the care of Montgomery area patients; and WHEREAS, born in Nashville, Tennessee, on January 20, 314 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2005 8th Day - February 24, 2005 1935, Dr. Porter attended the University of the South in Sewanee, Tennessee; Vanderbilt University and Vanderbilt University School of Medicine in Nashville, Tennessee; he served his country in the United States Navy in the Medical Corps; and WHEREAS, Dr. Porter was trained at Vanderbilt University Hospital, Duke University Hospital, University of Virginia Hospital, and The University of Alabama Medical Center; he has served as Clinical Instructor and Clinical Assistant Professor of Medicine at Vanderbilt University and The University of Alabama School of Medicine; and as Director of Medication Education at Montgomery Regional Medical Foundation; and WHEREAS, during his professional career, Dr. Porter has served as President of the Medical Staff and Advisory Board of St. Margaret’s Hospital in Montgomery; on the Blue Cross/Blue Shield of Alabama Board of Directors; and the University of the South Board of Trustees in Sewanee, Tennessee; and WHEREAS, Dr. Porter exemplifies the highest standards of professionalism and his dedication to his wife, Douglass, his family, church, community, and patients has earned for him the admiration and respect of all those with whom he is associated; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That we herein recognize March 4, 2005, as “Mac Porter Day” and commend Dr. Charles McGavock Porter as an exceptional physician who has made such a difference in people’s lives. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That a copy of this reso- lution shall be provided for appropriate presentation to Dr. Porter so that he may know of our respect and admiration of his contributions to mankind. COMMENDING STEPHEN BLAKE HARBISON ON OBTAINING THE RANK OF EAGLE SCOUT. WHEREAS, noted with highest commendation is the attain- ment of the rank of Eagle Scout, the highest rank in Boy Scouts of America, by Stephen Blake Harbison; and WHEREAS, born in Birmingham, Alabama, on August 21, 1986, Blake is the son of Stephen and Wava Harbison; he graduated from Bible Methodist Christian School at Chula Vista, Alabama, in 2004, where he was Captain of the school’s Bible Quiz Team for two years; he attends the Pilgrim Nazarene Church in Pell City, where he participates in the music program playing the saxophone; and WHEREAS, Blake Harbison was a member of the National Beta Club, nominated for Who’s Who in American High School students for three years, featured three years in the United States Achievement Academy, and All-American Scholars for two years; his poetry was published in A Celebration of Young Southern Poets; he also participated in photography competition, winning many state awards and second place in the National Competition at Bob Jones University; and WHEREAS, this coveted rank was earned through countless hours of hard work, diligence, and great perseverance to complete the required community service project and to fulfill the other stringent criteria for Eagle Scout status; Blake Harbison’s accomplishments will be recognized at an Eagle Scout Court of Honor on March 12, 2005; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That Stephen Blake Harbison is congratulated and commended for his outstanding achievement on obtaining the rank of Eagle Scout, and it is directed that he receive a copy of this resolution in highest admiration and with sincere best wishes for all future endeavors. COMMENDING THE 2004 AUBURN UNIVER- SITY FOOTBALL TEAM ON ITS 13-0 SEASON. WHEREAS, it is with great pride that we commend and congratulate the 2004 Auburn University Football Team upon its tremendous 13-0 season, thus bringing immense happiness to the local community and state and, in recognition thereof, the team members, the members of the coaching staff, and all of those individuals associated with the team are deserving of special public commendation; and WHEREAS, the Auburn Tigers won the SEC Championship, their first conference title since 1989 and first outright championship since 1987; and the 2005 Nokia Sugar Bowl, their third straight bowl win; Coach Tommy Tuberville won six Coach of the Year Awards; and WHEREAS, winning 15 straight games ties the third-longest winning streak in school history and marks the third-longest current winning streak in the nation; the Tigers also won four games over Associated Press Top 10 teams, the most of any Division I team, and played the fifth-toughest schedule in the nation as sorted by cumulative opposition; and WHEREAS, the Tigers ranked first in the nation in scoring defense, marking the first time since 1988 that they have led the nation in a statistical category, and they also finished fifth in total defense; and WHEREAS, ably led by Head Coach Tommy Tuberville and his assistant coaches, the 2004 Auburn Senior class includes Ronnie Brown, Jason Campbell, Silas Daniels, Bret Eddins, Derrick Graves, Bret Holliman, Jeremy Ingle, Doug Langenfeld, Danny Lindsey, Jay Ratliff, Sam Rives, Carlos Rogers, Junior Rosegreen, Mayo Sowell, Rich Trucks, Carnell Williams, Philip Yost, and Donnay Young; and WHEREAS, Auburn players set five career records and two single-season records; in addition to excelling in athletics, Auburn placed 17 student-athletes on the SEC Academic Honor Roll; and WHEREAS, the State of Alabama can be proud of athletic competitors of the caliber of the 2004 Auburn University Football Team who played every game in the spirit and tradition of good sportsmanship and each member of the team is to be praised for his integral part in achieving this coveted goal; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- 392 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2005 9th Day - March 1, 2005 BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That the 2004 Auburn University Football Team is recognized, honored, and commended for its outstanding 13-0 winning season and a copy of this resolution will be provided to Coach Tommy Tuberville in sincere tribute and esteem with best wishes for future success. RECOGNIZING THE MONTH OF MARCH AS THE SELMA TO MONTGOMERY MARCH/NATIONAL VOT- ING RIGHTS CELEBRATION MONTH AND THE WEEKEND OF MARCH 4-6, 2005, ON THE 40TH ANNIVERSARY OF THE VOTING RIGHTS MARCH IN ALABAMA. WHEREAS, on Sunday, March 7, 1965, citizens participating in a peaceful march while seeking their voting rights were beaten as they attempted to cross the Edmond Pettus Bridge in Selma, Alabama; and WHEREAS, on March 21, 1965, the Selma to Montgomery March brought international attention to the cause of voter regis- tration in the State of Alabama; and WHEREAS, over 25,000 people marched together in a fight for the right to vote, freely and fairly from any harassment or dis- crimination; and WHEREAS, due in part to the efforts of the participants in the Selma to Montgomery March, Congress promptly enacted the Voting Rights Act of 1965, thereby ensuring the right of all citizens to vote; and WHEREAS, the Selma to Montgomery March inspired people from nations all over the world, including South Africa and Poland, to proclaim and fight for their right to vote and is an international symbol for the right to vote; and WHEREAS, the Selma to Montgomery March solidified America as a true democracy by providing the impetus by which all citizens of the United States of America are allowed to exercise their basic constitutional right to vote; and 418 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2005 10th Day - March 3, 2005 WHEREAS, the rich history and fame surrounding the Selma to Montgomery March have had a tremendous impact on educating people about voting rights and have resulted in the promotion of tourism and economic development in the State of Alabama; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That we hereby recognize the month of March, in 2005, and in each succeeding year, as the Selma to Montgomery March/National Voting Rights Celebration Month in Alabama and that we further recognize the weekend of March 4-6 in 2005, on the 40th Anniversary of the historic voting rights march in Alabama. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That we urge the citizens of Alabama to reflect on the history surrounding the march and the tremendous impact it had making America a true democracy and creating a more fair and just society for all. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That we urge the U.S. Congress to renew the Voting Rights Act of 1965. Senator Sanders requested and received unanimous consent to suspend the provisions of Senate Rule 55 and the Resolution was adopted by the Senate.

HONORING DR. DENNIS L. IRELAND ON THE OCCASION OF HIS 75TH BIRTHDAY. WHEREAS, it is with great pride and admiration that we rec- ognize in a lasting and appropriate manner the 75th birthday of Dr. Dennis L. “Dan” Ireland of Birmingham, Alabama; and WHEREAS, born on March 17, 1930, Dr. Ireland graduated from Ensley High School in Birmingham and received a Bachelor of Arts Degree from Samford University, a Master of Divinity Degree from New Orleans Baptist Theological Seminary, and a Doctor of Di- vinity Degree from Samford University; and WHEREAS, with an enduring symbol of commitment to the Gospel Ministry, Dr. Ireland was ordained into the ministry on Au- gust 28, 1949, and has faithfully served as pastor of Jackson Memo- rial Baptist Church in LaFayette, Dolomite Baptist Church in Besse- mer, Eastside Baptist Church in Birmingham, First Baptist Church in Fort Payne, and Jackson Way Baptist Church in Huntsville before ac- cepting the position of Executive Director of the Alabama Citizens Action Program, serving from 1978 to the present; and WHEREAS, as an extension of his ministry, Dan Ireland has been involved in numerous denominational activities, including serv- ing as President of the Bessemer Baptist Pastor’s Conference and member and Chair of the Alabama Baptist State Convention Board of Missions, as well as serving on a number of committees for the con- vention, particularly in formulating the plans and format of Good News Alabama and the Bold Missions Thrust Committee; and WHEREAS, Dr. Ireland also has immeasurably contributed 590 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2005 13th Day - March 15, 2005 his energies, time, and many talents to numerous social, civic, and humanitarian endeavors; and WHEREAS, a devoted family man, Dan Ireland and his wife, the former Pauline Tucker, are the proud parents of a daughter and son-in-law, Denise and Fred K. Cypress, and a son and daughter-in- law, Jeffrey and Barbara Ireland, and are the doting grandparents of four grandchildren, David, Daniel, Michael, and Katie; and WHEREAS, Dr. Ireland has indeed lived life in reverence for God, in love and concern for others more than self, and in making friends of strangers he has met along life’s journey; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That Dr. Dennis L. Ireland is most heartily congratulated on the momentous occasion of his 75th birthday and, by copy of this resolution, we ex- tend to him sincere best wishes for continuing good health and God’s richest blessings. ENCOURAGING THE POSTING OF CLASS SIZE STATISTICS. WHEREAS, the Alabama State Board of Education passed class-size caps for grade levels K-12 during 1997-1998; and WHEREAS, parents, teachers, and the public at-large have a right to know whether teachers are being properly assigned to classes to meet these class-size caps and such reports, publicly posted, en- hance the accountability standards for K-12 education; now there- fore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That each lo- cal school system is encouraged to post actual enrollment statistics on the State Department of Education Internet site by class, grade, and school basis, not later than the 10th on-roll day. Such enrollment sta- tistics should be verified by the respective classroom teacher. Any changes in enrollment should also be posted by the 20th on-roll day and verified by the classroom teacher. The State Department of Edu- cation should cooperate with the local school system in implementing these accountability standards. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That a copy of this resolu- tion shall be sent to the State Superintendent of Education for distri- bution to each local school system. Senator Smitherman requested and received unanimous con- sent to suspend the provisions of Senate Rule 55 and the Resolution was adopted by the Senate.

COMMENDING THE STAFF OF SOUTHERN COMPANY FOR ITS 5-STAR MISSION OF EMPLOYER SUP- PORT FOR MEMBERS OF THE NATIONAL GUARD AND RE- SERVE. WHEREAS, it is with highest commendation that we com- mend the Staff of Southern Company for its 5-Star mission of Em- ployer Support for Members of the National Guard and Reserve; and WHEREAS, with this important step, Southern Company joins other employers in pledging that employment will not be denied because of service in the Guard and Reserve, career opportunities will not be limited because of military service, and employees will be granted leaves of absence consistent with existing laws without sac- rificing vacation; and WHEREAS, with the call for our men and women to fight the War Against Terrorism, mobilization places a strain upon the em- ployers and public servants who must endeavor to keep their busi- nesses and agencies functioning efficiently in the absence of these citizen-reservists while they fight for our country’s freedom; and WHEREAS, federal and state law imposes duties and obliga- tions upon employers of citizen-reservists that must be honored to en- able the citizen-reservists to perform their vital duties when mobi- lized in defense of this nation; MOURNING THE DEATH OF DR. HOWARD STANSELL BANTON, JR., OF UNION SPRINGS, ALABAMA. WHEREAS, recorded with a sense of deep sorrow and loss is the lamentable death of Dr. Howard Stansell Banton, Jr., of Union Springs, Alabama, on February 25, 2005, at the age of 83 years; and WHEREAS, Dr. Banton was a graduate of Birmingham- Southern College, The University of Alabama, and Washington Uni- versity Medical School; after completing his military service as a member of the United States Air Force during World War II, he be- gan medical practice in Union Springs, which lasted for 44 years until his retirement in 1992; and WHEREAS, with immeasurable humility and sense of pur- pose, Dr. Banton also dedicated his many talents as a Diplomat of the American Board of Family Practice, member of the American Medi- cal Association and Medical Association of the State of Alabama, and charter member of the Union Springs Exchange Club; and WHEREAS, he also was a parishioner of St. Pius X Catholic Church and an accomplished wildlife and nature photographer, a na- tionally recognized conservationist, and well-known for his love of turkey hunting and contagious sense of humor; and WHEREAS, in the death of Dr. Banton, the community, his loving family, and many friends have indeed suffered an inconsolable 598 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2005 13th Day - March 15, 2005 loss, yet his devotion and commitment in service to others stand as a lasting legacy and tribute to his memory; and WHEREAS, left to cherish the memory of Dr. Banton are his wife, Penelope P. Banton; sons, Dr. H. Stan Banton, III, and Cope (Ellen) Lawrence; daughters, Becky (Jerry) Cleveland and Lisa (Ran- dy) Helms; eight grandchildren and one great-granddaughter; and other devoted family members and friends; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That deepest sympathy is extended to the wife of Dr. Howard Stansell Banton, Jr., of Union Springs, Alabama, for whom a copy of this resolution is provided with our sincere condolence. Senator Little (T) requested and received unanimous consent to suspend the provisions of Senate Rule 55 and the Resolution was adopted by the Senate.

MOURNING THE DEATH OF MS. JANE GUL- LATT OF PHENIX CITY, ALABAMA. WHEREAS, it is with great sorrow and regret that we note the lamentable death of Ms. Jane Gullatt, a prominent resident of Phenix City, Alabama, and a former Phenix City Mayor and State Legislator, on March 8, 2005; and WHEREAS, Ms. Gullatt was a graduate of The University of Alabama, where she served as President of Phi Mu Sorority; Presi- REGULAR SESSION 599 13th Day - March 15, 2005 dent of Mortar Board, the highest senior women’s honorary society; and member of the “Golden Fifties” Club; and WHEREAS, she carried out her many duties and responsibil- ities in a highly efficient and professional manner as a newspaper journalist at The Tuscaloosa News, The Pensacola News, The Co- lumbus Enquirer, and The Phenix Citizen; in recognition of her edi- torial writing, Ms. Gullatt was the recipient of numerous prestigious awards, including the Golden Quill Award; and WHEREAS, with the interest of her fellow citizens always a priority, Ms. Gullatt served as an elected official for seventeen years, working tirelessly to make the Phenix City Community a better place to live for her family and many, many friends; and WHEREAS, included among her many professional respon- sibilities was service on the Phenix City Council, as the first female Mayor of Phenix City, a member of the Alabama House of Represen- tatives, and valued member of the Alabama Commission on Higher Education; and WHEREAS, Ms. Gullatt, a lifelong and faithful member of Trinity United Methodist Church, was active in numerous civic, char- itable, youth-related and government-related affairs at the local and state levels and, during her lifetime, was recognized by many organi- zations for outstanding achievement, good citizenship, distinguished service, and her journalistic skills; and WHEREAS, left to cherish the memory of Ms. Gullatt are a brother, Claude Bertram “Bert” Gullatt, III; sister, Judy Gullatt (Ed- die) Ezell; and other devoted family members and friends; now there- fore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That the memory of Ms. Jane Gullatt of Phenix City, Alabama, will live for- ever in the hearts and minds of all those whose lives she touched and it is directed that a copy of this resolution be presented to her family with our sincere condolence. Senator Little (T) requested and received unanimous consent to suspend the provisions of Senate Rule 55 and the Resolution was adopted by the Senate.

MOURNING THE DEATH OF LOUISE PITTMAN. WHEREAS, recorded with a sense of deep sorrow and loss is the death of Louise Pittman on February 26, 2005, at the age of 90 years; and WHEREAS, born October 27, 1914, in Tallapoosa County, Louise Pittman earned a Bachelor’s Degree from the University of Montevallo and a Master’s Degree from the University of Chicago; and WHEREAS, from 1935 to 1988, Louise Pittman was a child welfare advocate; in 1964, she was named Director of the Depart- ment of Human Resources’ Division of Family and Children’s Ser- vices; one of the highlights of her career was her effort to push for legislation requiring mandatory reporting of child abuse cases; and REGULAR SESSION 603 13th Day - March 15, 2005 WHEREAS, a real pioneer, Louise Pittman also is credited with strengthening child-care laws such as licensing day-care centers and requiring specific training procedures for those hired to look after children in Alabama; and WHEREAS, after her retirement, Louise Pittman continued to serve as a volunteer for child welfare groups such as Child Protect, Gift of Life, Montgomery County Department of Human Resources, and Voices for Alabama’s Children; and WHEREAS, among the many awards received for her untir- ing work, Louise Pittman was named the Montgomery Advertiser 2000 Citizen of the Year, 1993 Pioneer in Social Work, 1991 Women of Achievement Award, and 1982 Social Worker of the Year; and WHEREAS, a champion for the health and well-being of countless Alabama boys and girls, Louise Pittman earned the admira- tion and respect of all those with whom she was associated; her death has indeed left a deep void in the life of the community; now there- fore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That in sad- ness and regret the death of Louise Pittman is hereby recorded, and sincerest sympathy is extended to her family for whom a copy of this resolution shall be provided. Senator Dixon requested and received unanimous consent to suspend the provisions of Senate Rule 55 and the Resolution was adopted by the Senate.

COMMENDING FORMER POLICE CHIEF DOU- GLAS J. JEFFERSON FOR OUTSTANDING PROFESSIONAL ACHIEVEMENTS. 604 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2005 13th Day - March 15, 2005 WHEREAS, noted with highest commendation is the long- time, dedicated career of Police Chief Douglas J. Jefferson, who served with devotion as a law enforcement officer with the Birming- ham Police Department and the Vestavia Hills Police Department, in- cluding service as a Patrolman, Detective, Sergeant, Lieutenant, and Acting Chief of Police before his appointment to Police Chief from 1983 and until his retirement on February 28, 2005; and WHEREAS, Chief Jefferson is a skilled and dedicated profes- sional with an extensive background and training in all aspects of law enforcement and served long and well in his charge to defend the peace and uphold the law to the good and well-being of his fellow cit- izens; and WHEREAS, he is a graduate of the prestigious FBI National Academy and FBI Law Enforcement Executive Development School at Quantico and attended the Dignitary Protection School in Wash- ington, D.C., conducted by the United States Secret Service; and WHEREAS, in recognition of his many achievements, Chief Jefferson was selected “Officer of the Year” by the Shades Mountain Optimist Club and Vestavia Hills Exchange Club and recipient of the Law Enforcement Commendation Medal; and WHEREAS, additionally, he was appointed by former Attor- ney General Bill Pryor to serve on his Law Enforcement Advisory Committee and by Governor Bob Riley to serve on the 17-member Alabama Peace Officers Standards and Training Commission; and WHEREAS, his devotion to duty, personal integrity, outgo- ing personality, and ability to relate to others fostered a spirit of friendship, respect, and trust among his fellow officers and others who knew him; and WHEREAS, indeed, Chief Jefferson has demonstrated throughout his tenure as a public servant that his heart reaches out be- yond his family and into the community; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That on the occasion of his retirement, and in recognition of outstanding service as Police Chief for Vestavia Hills, Alabama, highest commendation is hereby accorded Police Chief Douglas J. Jefferson, for whom a copy of this resolution is provided with sincere best wishes for every future happiness and success. DESIGNATING A PORTION OF INTERSTATE 85 IN LEE COUNTY THE RAY BASS HIGHWAY. WHEREAS, Mr. Ray Bass, the Chief Engineer of the Ala- bama Department of Transportation, has served the Alabama High- way Department and its successor agency, the Department of Trans- portation, in various leadership capacities over his 48-year tenure, which began in 1957; and WHEREAS, the first major project Ray Bass oversaw was the construction of that portion of Interstate 85 running east of the Lee- Macon County Line in Lee County to mile post 63, located east of the intersection of I-85 and U.S. Highway 431; and WHEREAS, over his distinguished career, Ray Bass served three terms as Highway Director of the Alabama Highway Depart- ment, including two consecutive terms as highway director; and WHEREAS, for the past 10 years, Ray Bass has ably served as the Department of Transportation Chief Engineer; and WHEREAS, Ray Bass personally and professionally wit- nessed the implementation of the Interstate Highway System in this state; and WHEREAS, it is both appropriate and desirable to recognize the public service of Ray Bass in a tangible and permanent manner; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That we hereby designate that portion of Interstate 85 beginning at the Macon- Lee County Line and proceeding east in Lee County to mile marker 63 east of the intersection of I-85 and U.S. Highway 431 as the Ray Bass Highway; and we direct that a copy of this resolution shall be provided to Ray Bass as an expression of our gratitude for his contri- butions to the modernization of the highway system in Alabama. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the appropriate state and local officials are requested to place and maintain signs and markers recognizing the Ray Bass Highway. WHEREAS, during the World War II effort, almost 1,000 Af- rican-American aviators, whose responsibility would be to escort America’s bombers over enemy territory, studied at historic Tuskeg- ee Institute and trained at Moton Field, Tuskegee Army Air Corp Field, and elsewhere in America; and WHEREAS, these aviators, who became known as the Tuske- gee Airmen, distinguished themselves in combat over the skies of North Africa and Europe during World War II, flying more than 15,000 sorties and destroying more than 450 enemy planes; and WHEREAS, in tribute to the valor and class of these distin- guished aviators, the Tuskegee Chapter of the Negro Airmen Interna- tional, Inc. hosts an annual Tuskegee, Alabama Memorial Day fly-in, attracting minority pilots and supporters from across the United States; and WHEREAS, in tribute to the courage and heroism of the Tuskegee Airmen, Tuskegee University as of April 20-22, 2001, has launched an annual convocation in honor of the Tuskegee Airmen; and WHEREAS, it is proper to especially note Lieutenant Colonel Retired Herbert Eugene Carter, a member of the first graduating class of the 99th Squadron, who served with distinction in the original 99th Pursuit Squadron and who is a true American patriot to whom special honor, salutes, and sincere gratitude are due; and WHEREAS, it is also fitting to note the accomplishments of other surviving Tuskegee Airmen living in Alabama and throughout the nation and provide special tribute to the families of the 66 who died during the war and others who have died subsequently; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That, in highest recognition of their significant contributions to our nation and the freedoms we all enjoy, we heartily commend the Tuskegee Air- men, Tuskegee University, and all Tuskegee Airmen Support Person- nel. Additionally, without reservation, we declare our strong and steadfast support for the establishment of the Tuskegee Airmen Mu- seum and encourage all state agencies to cooperate with the National Park Service and the Tuskegee Institute National Park Site to support 810 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2005 27th Day - April 27, 2005 development of this invaluable educational facility as an enduring and appropriate memorial to these brave Americans. DESIGNATING MAY 1 THROUGH MAY 7, 2005, AS LIVING WILL WEEK. WHEREAS, the death of a 41-year-old Florida woman who had no written advance health care directives that specified her health care preferences has spun a fierce debate over end-of-life decisions; and WHEREAS, by preparing a living will, most Alabamians can avoid situations as were created by the Florida case; and WHEREAS, only 36 percent of Americans, most of whom are elderly, have living wills; and WHEREAS, the Florida case has caused Americans of all ag- es to realize the importance of end-of-life planning; and WHEREAS, a living will allows people the opportunity to di- rect their own care with written instructions in the event one becomes critically ill and unable to communicate whether to use life-sustain- ing measures; and WHEREAS, Alabamians 19 years of age and older are en- couraged to make clear advance medical directives by preparing a living will; and WHEREAS, a living will form can be accessed at www.legis- lature.state.al.us/CodeofAlabama/1975/22-8A-4.htm; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That we hereby designate May 1 through May 7, 2005, as Living Will Week in Alabama. WHEREAS, it is with great personal pride and pleasure that Mr. and Mrs. Raymond Elliott of Prattville, Alabama, are honored and congratulated on the occasion of their 50th Wedding Anniversa- ry, August 19, 2005, and will celebrate with family and friends at the University Church of Christ in Montgomery, Alabama, on July 30, 2005; and WHEREAS, the former Virginia Ruth Slaughter and Billy Raymond Elliott began their long courtship at Montgomery Bible College (now Faulkner University) and enjoyed their first date at Jas- mine Hills on a sunny afternoon in 1954; and WHEREAS, since that time, Raymond, a minister in the Church of Christ, and Virginia, whose talents are best exhibited in her role as a homemaker, have spent their lives in service and ministry for their Lord and Savior Jesus Christ; and WHEREAS, Mr. and Mrs. Elliott have remained steadfastly faithful each to the other for more than 50 years and to all those who have witnessed their commitment to the ideals of marriage, their last- ing partnership indeed serves as an enviable example of trust and de- votion; and WHEREAS, contributing significantly toward the good and 826 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2005 27th Day - April 27, 2005 well-being of their fellow citizens in civic and community affairs, Mr. and Mrs. Elliott continue to enjoy life to the fullest, rejoicing in the love of their three sons, a daughter, and nine wonderful grandchil- dren; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That Mr. and Mrs. Raymond Elliott of Prattville, Alabama, are congratulated on the occasion of their 50th Wedding Anniversary; commended for achieving a long and happy marriage blessed with children and rich in friendships; and, by copy of this resolution, they are extended sin- cere best wishes for continued happiness and good health. URGING THE NORTH CAROLINA LEGISLA- TURE TO ENACT LEGISLATION TO REQUIRE APPLICANTS FOR A DRIVER’S LICENSE TO PROVE THEY ARE LEGALLY IN THIS COUNTRY. WHEREAS, the State of North Carolina is one of only a very few states that do not explicitly require applicants for a driver’s li- cense to prove they are legally present in this country; and WHEREAS, North Carolina has become a magnet for illegal immigrants seeking driver’s licenses under false pretenses; and WHEREAS, these illegal immigrants then move to another state, including Alabama, and present the driver’s license as a legal form of identification to obtain benefits from the other state; and WHEREAS, industry in Alabama has suffered greatly due to the growing number of illegal immigrants obtaining jobs and benefits that should be going to the residents of this state; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That we hereby urge the Legislature of North Carolina to enact appropriate legislation requiring an applicant for a driver’s license to prove that the applicant is legally present in this country. BE IT RESOLVED FURTHER, That a copy of this resolu- tion be sent forthwith to the Legislature of North Carolina that it may know of our deep concerns in this matter. DESIGNATING THE NORTHERN BOULEVARD BETWEEN COLISEUM BOULEVARD AND THE LOWER WE- TUMPKA ROAD AS GUNNERY SERGEANT STEPHEN L. BRYSON BOULEVARD. WHEREAS, it is with great pride and admiration that we name the Northern Boulevard between Coliseum Boulevard and the Lower Wetumpka Road the Gunnery Sergeant Stephen L. Bryson Boulevard; and WHEREAS, Sergeant Bryson provided unexcelled service and made incalculable sacrifices and contributions to the Armed Forces while he served as a Marine from 1984 until his untimely death in a United States Marine Corps tanker plane crash on January 9, 2002; and WHEREAS, Sergeant Bryson, known for his superior techni- cal skills as a Flight Engineer, accumulated over 6,200 flight hours during his exemplary service which included participation in Exer- cise Eager Mace in Kuwait; Exercise Bright Star in Benisues, Egypt; Operation Northern Watch in Incirlik, Turkey; and finally, Operation Enduring Freedom in Jacobabad, Pakistan; and WHEREAS, Sergeant Bryson’s personal awards include the Good Conduct Medal, Armed Forces Expeditionary Medal, Kuwait Liberation Medal, Southwest Asia Service Medal, National Defense Medal, and Humanitarian Service Medal; and WHEREAS, Sergeant Bryson was a true exemplar of those brave men and women whose sense of duty and dedication in defense of others represent the ultimate in personal sacrifice, and the heroism he exhibited will never be forgotten; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That the Northern Boulevard between Coliseum Boulevard and the Lower Wetumpka Road is hereby designated Gunnery Sergeant Stephen L. Bryson Boulevard; appropriate authorities are encouraged to erect and maintain signs and markers specifying this designation of honor. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That we hereby request the appropriate officials to install and maintain signs or markers desig- nating the Gunnery Sergeant Stephen L. Bryson Boulevard. ADOPTING THE REPORT OF THE JUDICIAL COMPENSATION COMMISSION TO THE 2005 REGULAR SESSION OF THE LEGISLATURE OF ALABAMA. WHEREAS, the report of the Judicial Compensation Commission has been duly filed with the Legislature within the first five days of this, the 2005 Regular Session of the Legislature of Alabama; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALABAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That the report of the Judicial Compensation Commission, made to the 2005 Regular Session of the Legislature of Alabama, is adopted and confirmed in accordance with Amendments 328 and 426 of the Constitution of the State of Alabama of 1901. The report stated in part, "It is, therefore, recommended to the Legislature to reinstate the provision of the Investment of Justice Act as it applied to circuit and district court judges only which were removed by Act No. 2004-636 in an effort to alleviate the gross disparity in pay among the judges of the state. It is further recommended that the salaries of the circuit and district judges to be paid from the state treasury be fixed to include an increase above the base salary to reflect 1.25 percent for every year they have served as judge to a maximum of 25 percent." On motion of Representative Clark, the resolution, HJR583, was adopted.

To provide for salary increases for certain officers em- ployed by the Department of Public Safety. The Standing Committee on Finance and Taxation General Fund reported the following substitute for the Bill, SB85, to wit: SUBSTITUTE FOR SB85 A BILL TO BE ENTITLED AN ACT To provide for salary increases for certain officers employed by the Department of Public Safety. BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALABAMA: Section 1. (a) Effective with the first payday on or after June 1, 2006, state troopers and corporals and such other comparable clas- sifications of arresting officers employed by the Department of Pub- lic Safety shall receive a four step, 10 percent, salary increase; ser- geants and lieutenants and such other comparable classifications of arresting officers employed by the department shall receive a three step, seven and one-half percent, salary increase; and captains and higher ranking officers and such other comparable classifications of arresting officers employed by the department shall receive a two step, five percent, salary increase. The salary increases provided herein shall not affect normal annual merit raise considerations. (b) The Director of the State Personnel Department shall re- vise the classifications and the schedule of rates set forth in the pay plan for employees employed by the Department of Public Safety to reflect the increases provided in subsection (a) and shall send the re- vised classifications and pay plan to the State Comptroller, who shall issue warrants in accordance therewith.

STRONGLY URGING THE DEPARTMENT OF INDUSTRIAL RELATIONS TO OBEY AND ENFORCE STATE COAL MINING LAWS. GREG PAPPAS, Clerk. On motion of Senator Smitherman, the Senate concurred in and adopted the following House amendment to the Resolution, SJR19, the title of which is set out in the foregoing Message from the House, to wit: SUBSTITUTE FOR SJR19 SJR19 STRONGLY URGING THE DEPARTMENT OF INDUSTRIAL RELATIONS TO OBEY AND ENFORCE STATE COAL MINING LAWS. WHEREAS, from 2001 to present, there have been 21 fatali- ties in the Alabama mining industry; and WHEREAS, currently there are 2.4 mine inspectors in the Department of Industrial Relations Mine Safety Program, down from 6.5 in 2001, and only 791 of the lawfully required 1,705 inspections were completed in 2004; and WHEREAS, there are 509 mines in Alabama of which 9 are operating underground coal mines, the 509:3 ratio of total mines to mine inspectors in Alabama is deplorable when compared to other states: Kentucky has 519:33, Ohio has 95:29, Pennsylvania has 454:70, and West Virginia has 352:32; and WHEREAS, Chapter 9 of Title 25 of the Code of Alabama 1975, the “Alabama Coal Mine Safety Law of 1975,” is a comprehen- sive body of statutes with the stated purpose of providing “reasonable laws to promote the safety and health of those engaged in the mining of coal and for the protection and preservation of property”; and WHEREAS, specifically, Section 25-9-7 of the code provides 494 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2006 9th Day - Februay 7, 2006 that the “duties of mine inspectors are to make examinations of mines” and Section 25-9-20 mandates that coal mines be completely inspected at least every 45 days and “more often if necessary”; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That in the interest of public safety and the health, safety, and protection of the coal miners working in the state, the Alabama Department of Indus- trial Relations is strongly and seriously urged to obey and enforce state coal mining laws. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That a copy of this resolu- tion be immediately provided to the Director of the Alabama Depart- ment of Industrial Relations and the Director of the Division of Min- ing and Reclamation of the Alabama Department of Industrial Relations as an indication of our profound sentiment on this issue.

URGING MUNICIPALITIES IN JEFFERSON COUNTY NOT TO INCREASE FEES PAID TO STORM WASTE MANAGEMENT AUTHORITY AND REJECT ANY PRIOR DE- CISION MADE TO INCREASE SUCH FEES. WHEREAS, several municipalities in Jefferson County have been requested to increase fees paid to the Storm Waste Management Authority (SWMA) pursuant to a new draft permit under consider- ation by the Alabama Department of Environmental Management (ADEM); and 218 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2006 4th Day - January 19, 2006 WHEREAS, local municipal governments are authorized, but not required, to participate in the program of the authority pursuant to Title 11, Chapter 89C, Code of Alabama 1975, as one alternative for the management of stormwater in compliance with the EPA National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES); and WHEREAS, another alternative for NPDES compliance is a cooperative government program in which ADEM would work with local governments in meeting their compliance issues; and WHEREAS, ADEM has a long history of working with EPA- regulated local entities to ensure that the entities are fully informed on compliance requirements; and WHEREAS, merely participating in the SWMA program does not relieve any municipality of its stormwater liability issues re- lated to NPDES compliance; and WHEREAS, a local governmental entity can obtain an indi- vidual NPDES water permit without SWMA participation; and WHEREAS, considering the alternatives to NPDES compli- ance, the SWMA should be considered an additional, not exclusive, method of achieving compliance; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That the mu- nicipalities in Jefferson County participating in the Storm Waste Management Authority (SWMA) for NPDES compliance are hereby urged to resist increased SWMA participation fees, and to reject or void any prior decision to pay increased SWMA participation fees until all options, including a voluntary cooperative government pro- gram, are considered for NPDES issues. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That a copy of this resolu- tion be provided to ADEM and to the governing body of each affect- ed municipality. SUPPORTING GOVERNOR RILEY’S CALL FOR A BOYCOTT OF TRAVEL TO ARUBA. WHEREAS, on May 30, 2005, Natalee Holloway, an 18- year-old Alabama citizen, disappeared on the island of Aruba; and WHEREAS, for many months now the citizens of Alabama have been both saddened by Natalee’s disappearance and inspired by her family and their resolve to find the truth and find their daughter; and WHEREAS, as the months passed, it became increasingly clear that Aruba’s investigation of Natalee’s disappearance has been plagued with an unacceptable amount of missteps, miscommunica- tions, and inconsistencies, as numerous suspects have been detained, but then released, without the benefit of gaining any new information that has helped find our missing fellow American; and WHEREAS, Governor Riley has recognized with apprecia- REGULAR SESSION 233 4th Day - January 19, 2006 tion the efforts of many private citizens of Aruba for their assistance in the search for Natalee; however, on November 17, 2005, after care- ful consideration of the official actions of the government of Aruba, Governor Riley, joined by Natalee’s family, urged all Americans to avoid travel to Aruba; and WHEREAS, subsequently, on November 22, 2005, Governor Riley also asked other Governors to urge their citizens to avoid travel to Aruba in hopes that a boycott would cause the Aruban people to demand that their public officials conduct the investigation of Nata- lee’s disappearance in a more careful, thorough, and appropriate manner; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That the Legislature heartily supports Governor Riley in this difficult but well-founded decision to urge a boycott of travel to Aruba. BE IT RESOLVED FURTHER, That the Legislature provide a copy of this resolution to Governor Riley as a show of its support of his actions. On motion of Senator French, the Resolution was adopted by the Senate.

URGING THE STATE BOARD OF EDUCATION AND THE ALABAMA DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC HEALTH TO DEVELOP A PROGRAM TO EDUCATE STUDENTS ON MEN- INGOCOCCAL DISEASE. WHEREAS, meningococcal disease is an extremely serious illness that is caused by bacterial infection; and WHEREAS, meningococcal bacteria can cause meningitis, an inflammation of the lining of the brain and spinal cord, or sepsis, an infection of the bloodstream, and can cause death or other system- ic permanent sequlae; and WHEREAS, vaccination against meningococcal disease may successfully reduce the disease’s incidence in the United States; and WHEREAS, the Centers for Disease Control, Advisory Com- mittee on Immunization Practices, recommends meningitis vaccina- tion or Menactra, at 11 and 12 years of age, 15 years of age, and for college freshmen living in dormitories; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That we hereby urge the State Department of Education in collaboration with the Alabama Department of Public Health to educate parents of stu- dents entering the 6th, 10th, and 12th grades about meningococcal disease, including the causes and symptoms, how it is spread, and how to obtain additional information about the disease and the avail- ability, effectiveness, and risk of vaccination against the disease, for five consecutive years beginning with the school year 2006/2007. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That a copy of this resolu- tion be sent forthwith to the State Department of Education and the REGULAR SESSION 255 5th Day - January 24, 2006 Alabama Department of Public Health that they may know of our concerns in this matter. WHEREAS, it is with highest commendation and esteem that Mr. Jack Faris is recognized for his outstanding professional achieve- ments as President and CEO of the National Federation of Indepen- dent Business (NFIB), where he has served as its President since 1992 and is retiring in February 2006; and WHEREAS, Mr. Faris is ranked as the most influential small business leader in Washington by Fortune Small Business magazine and, as President of NFIB, is the leading spokesperson for small busi- ness in America; and WHEREAS, during his distinguished tenure with NFIB, Mr. Faris has provided exemplary skills and leadership for its 600,000 members nationwide, including more than 12,000 in Alabama, to make sure that their concerns are known to policy makers in Wash- ington and all 50 state capitals; and WHEREAS, with his remarkable abilities and steadfast direc- tion, Mr. Faris has served as a member of the National Commission on Economic Growth and Tax Reform and was recently named by President Bush to the President’s Export Council; and WHEREAS, indeed, the personal endeavors displayed by Mr. Faris have reflected great credit upon the State of Alabama; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That in rec- ognition of his outstanding professional career and service to the State of Alabama, highest commendation and congratulations are hereby accorded Mr. Jack Faris, President and CEO of the National Federation of Independent Business, for whom a copy of this resolu- tion is provided with sincere regard and best wishes for a gratifying retirement. The report stated in part, “It is, therefore, recommended to the Legislature to reinstate the provision of the Investment of Justice Act as it applied to circuit and district court judges only which were re- moved by Act No. 2004-636 in an effort to alleviate the gross dispar- ity in pay among the judges of the state. MOURNING THE DEATH OF MR. GODWIN O. LONG. WHEREAS, it is with deepest sorrow and regret that we record the lamentable death of Mr. Godwin O. “Pop” Long, a prom- inent resident of Smith Station, Alabama, on January 17, 2006, at the age of 82 years; and WHEREAS, Mr. Long’s family moved to Smith Station in 1938 and, after graduation from high school, he served his country in the Army Transportation Corps during World War II and married his wife of 51 years, Edna “Sis” Carden Long, who preceded him in death; and REGULAR SESSION 409 7th Day - January 31, 2006 WHEREAS, he also devoted considerable time in service to his community as a member of the Lee County Board of Education for 32 years, 22 of which he served as President; a charter member and board member of the Smith Station Athletic Association; a mem- ber of the Smith Station Ruritan Club and Smith Station Water Au- thority; and as President of the Board of the Lee County Farm Bu- reau; and WHEREAS, as a highly principled and dedicated business- man, he always exhibited excellence as the owner and operator of G. O. Long Builders, Incorporated, for 10 years; and was a faithful member of Smith Station Baptist Church for 60 years, where he was a devoted deacon and served as its treasurer for 24 years; and WHEREAS, indeed, throughout his lifetime, Mr. Long exhib- ited a consuming interest in the welfare and well-being of his beloved family, his community, and his fellowman, and his death has left an unfathomable void in the hearts of all those whose lives he touched through genuine care and concern; and WHEREAS, left to cherish the memory of Mr. Long are his wife, Jackie Henderson Long; three daughters, Leslie (Wayne) Echols, Fonda (Mark) Carter, and Nicole (Don) Farley; son, Ray- mond O. (Beth) Long; and other devoted family members and friends; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That we grievously mourn the death of Mr. Godwin O. Long of Smith Station, Alabama, and, by copy of this resolution to his wife, we extend our heartfelt sympathy and sincere condolence. ENCOURAGING THE STUDY OF THE BIBLE IN SCHOOLS. WHEREAS, the United States Supreme Court has declared: “It certainly may be said that the Bible is worthy of study for its liter- ary and historic qualities. Nothing we have said here indicates that such study of the Bible or of religion, when presented objectively as a part of a secular program of education, may not be effected consis- tently with the First Amendment”; and WHEREAS, the United States Supreme Court has also stated that it is not unconstitutional for the Bible to be used in the appropri- ate study of subjects such as literature, history, civilization, ethics, and similar disciplines; and WHEREAS, the State of Alabama Department of Educa- tions’s Subject and Personnel Code currently lists a course in the Bi- ble as Literature as an approved elective; and WHEREAS, the study of the Bible can offer a fundamental understanding of the influence of the Bible on literature, history, law, and American community life and culture; and WHEREAS, the study of the Bible can provide a greater knowledge of Middle Eastern history, geography, religion, and poli- tics; and WHEREAS, without imposing the doctrines of any particular religious sect, such studies can be used to inform the students of Al- abama of the importance of religion in world and national history; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That we strongly encourage the study of the Bible as an elective in city, coun- ty, or other local schools and in private schools in a manner not in- consistent with the Constitution of the United States of America and the Constitution of Alabama of 1901, in order to promote academic excellence and cultural literacy. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That if a local board of edu- cation wishes to develop and implement the study of the Bible as an elective course, the course should meet all State Board of Education standards for district-approved electives. REGULAR SESSION 411 7th Day - January 31, 2006 BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That a copy of this resolu- tion be transmitted to the State Superintendent of Education, so that its contents may be known to the superintendent of each local public school system. STRONGLY URGING THE DEPARTMENT OF INDUSTRIAL RELATIONS TO OBEY AND ENFORCE STATE COAL MINING LAWS. GREG PAPPAS, Clerk. On motion of Senator Smitherman, the Senate concurred in and adopted the following House amendment to the Resolution, SJR19, the title of which is set out in the foregoing Message from the House, to wit: SUBSTITUTE FOR SJR19 SJR19 STRONGLY URGING THE DEPARTMENT OF INDUSTRIAL RELATIONS TO OBEY AND ENFORCE STATE COAL MINING LAWS. WHEREAS, from 2001 to present, there have been 21 fatali- ties in the Alabama mining industry; and WHEREAS, currently there are 2.4 mine inspectors in the Department of Industrial Relations Mine Safety Program, down from 6.5 in 2001, and only 791 of the lawfully required 1,705 inspections were completed in 2004; and WHEREAS, there are 509 mines in Alabama of which 9 are operating underground coal mines, the 509:3 ratio of total mines to mine inspectors in Alabama is deplorable when compared to other states: Kentucky has 519:33, Ohio has 95:29, Pennsylvania has 454:70, and West Virginia has 352:32; and WHEREAS, Chapter 9 of Title 25 of the Code of Alabama 1975, the “Alabama Coal Mine Safety Law of 1975,” is a comprehen- sive body of statutes with the stated purpose of providing “reasonable laws to promote the safety and health of those engaged in the mining of coal and for the protection and preservation of property”; and WHEREAS, specifically, Section 25-9-7 of the code provides 494 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2006 9th Day - Februay 7, 2006 that the “duties of mine inspectors are to make examinations of mines” and Section 25-9-20 mandates that coal mines be completely inspected at least every 45 days and “more often if necessary”; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That in the interest of public safety and the health, safety, and protection of the coal miners working in the state, the Alabama Department of Indus- trial Relations is strongly and seriously urged to obey and enforce state coal mining laws. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That a copy of this resolu- tion be immediately provided to the Director of the Alabama Depart- ment of Industrial Relations and the Director of the Division of Min- ing and Reclamation of the Alabama Department of Industrial Relations as an indication of our profound sentiment on this issue.

CONDEMNING CHURCH ARSONS AND EXPRESSING SYMPATHY FOR A CHURCH BURNING, URG- ING SWIFT PUNISHMENT FOR THE PERPETRATORS, AND EXTENDING CONDOLENCES TO ALL CHURCH CONGREGA- TIONS AFFECTED. WHEREAS, from 4:30 p.m. on February 2, 2006, to 5:00 a.m. on February 3, 2006, five churches in Bibb County were intentionally burned in what fire investigators are calling the worst incidence of church arson since the outbreak of over 100 church fires in the 1990s; and WHEREAS, in addition to the despicable acts of one or more hateful and cowardly arsonists, a sixth church, New Harmony Baptist Church in Chilton County, also tragically sustained fire damage, but it was determined that the Chilton County church fire was not an act of arson; and 522 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2006 9th Day - Februay 7, 2006 WHEREAS, the spate of fires damaged or destroyed Reho- beth Baptist Church, Ashby Baptist Church, Old Union Baptist Church, Pleasant Sabine Baptist Church, and Antioch Baptist Church in Bibb County, and New Harmony Baptist Church in Chilton Coun- ty, disrupting the lives of about 550 members of the congregations of all churches combined; and WHEREAS, it has been reported that on Tuesday, February 7, 2006, that fire erupted at four more rural Alabama churches, and arson is suspected concerning Dancy Baptist Church, south of Aliceville in Pickens County, Spring Valley Baptist Church, near Emelle in Sumter County, Morning Star Baptist Church near Boligee in Greene County, and Galilee Baptist Church near Panola in Sumter County; and WHEREAS, a motive or motives have yet to be attributed to these senseless acts of destruction and violence; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That we hereby condemn these deplorable acts of arson and support federal and state law enforcement and the judicial system in the swift capture and punishment of the perpetrator or perpetrators of these heinous acts. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That we express our deepest heartfelt sympathy and condolences for the church members of all of the churches affected by this tragic string of events. Senator Singleton requested and received unanimous consent to suspend the provisions of Senate Rule 55 and the Resolution was adopted by the Senate.

DESIGNATING MARCH 4, 2006, AS NATIONAL ASSOCIATION FOR THE ADVANCEMENT OF COLORED PEOPLE YOUTH AND COLLEGE DAY. WHEREAS, we are pleased to designate March 4, 2006, as National Association for the Advancement of Colored People Youth and College Day in Alabama; and WHEREAS, the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP) Youth and College Division, founded March 4, 1936, will be celebrating its 70th Birthday; and WHEREAS, under the guidance of its first National Youth Director, Juanita Jackson Mitchell, the NAACP Youth and College Division has been known as a strong presence in every aspect of advancement of young people since its inception; and WHEREAS, under the guidance of the NAACP, some of its early leaders like Ruby Hurley and Gloster B. Current have led the nation in youth development, since the first Annual Student Conference at Virginia Union University, in Richmond, Virginia, March 29-31, 1940; and WHEREAS, the Montgomery Youth Council was part of the Montgomery Bus Boycott under the leadership of their advisor, Mrs. Rosa Parks; and WHEREAS, the Youth and College sit-in movement in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, August 1958, initiated a period of intense student activism throughout the South in the 1960s; and WHEREAS, the NAACP State Conferences, Branches, Youth Councils, and College Chapters across the country will be participating in the 70th Celebration and it is most fitting to recognize this momentous occasion; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That we are 592 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2006 11th Day - Februay 14, 2006 honored to designate March 4, 2006, as the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People Youth and College Day in Alabama and do further direct that a copy of this resolution shall be provided for appropriate presentation with our sincere tribute and praise. APPLYING TO THE UNITED STATES CON- GRESS FOR A CONVENTION TO PROPOSE AN AMENDMENT TO THE CONSTITUTION OF THE UNITED STATES. BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That this Legislature, pursuant to Article V of the Constitution of the United States, hereby makes application to the Congress of the United States to call a convention for the purpose of adopting the following amendment to the Constitution of the United States: Proposed Amendment: Section 1. This amendment may be cited as the “Marriage 770 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2006 14th Day - February 22, 2006 Protection Amendment.” Section 2. Marriage in the United States shall consist only of the union of a man and a woman. Neither this Constitution, nor the constitution of any State, shall be construed to require that marriage or the legal incidents thereof be conferred upon any union other than of a man and a woman. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That this application by the Legislature of the State of Alabama constitutes a continuing application in accordance with Article V of the Constitution of the United States until at least two-thirds of the legislatures of the several states have made similar applications pursuant to Article V. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That since this method of proposing amendments to the Constitution has never been completed to the point of calling a convention and no interpretation of the power of the states in the exercise of this right has ever been made by any court or any qualified tribunal, and since the exercise of the power is a matter of basic sovereign right and the interpretation thereof is primarily in the sovereign government making the exercise, and since the power to use the right in full also carries the power to use the right in part, the Legislature of the State of Alabama interprets Article V to mean that if two-thirds of the states make application for a convention to propose an identical amendment to the Constitution for ratification with a limitation that such an amendment would be the only matter before it; that such a convention would have power only to propose the specified amendment and would be limited to such a proposal; and would not have power to vary the text thereof or propose other amendments on the same or a different proposition. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That a duly attested copy of this resolution be immediately transmitted to the Secretary of the Senate of the United States, the Clerk of the House of Representatives of the United States, to each member of the Alabama Congressional Delegation, and to each house of each State Legislature in the United States. COMMENDING MRS. RHODA VAUGHN FOR OUTSTANDING PROFESSIONAL ACHIEVEMENTS. WHEREAS, it is with highest commendation and esteem that Mrs. Rhoda Vaughn is recognized on the occasion of her retirement, April 1, 2006, from The University of Alabama, where she has worked with professionalism for 28 years; and WHEREAS, a native of Birmingham, Alabama, she gradu- ated from Canton Academy in Mississippi; attended Trevecca Col- lege in Tennessee; and pursued courses from The University of Ala- bama’s External Degree Program; and WHEREAS, Mrs. Vaughn has worked as a member of the Athletics Department since 1981, including Tide Pride; and, since 1993, she has clearly demonstrated her extraordinary ability and seemingly unlimited capacity for work through her diligence and REGULAR SESSION 833 15th Day - February 23, 2006 devotion to those she has served during her distinguished tenure as Director of the Athletic Ticket Office since 1993; and WHEREAS, indeed, she carried out her many duties and responsibilities in a highly efficient manner, solved problems, offered help and moral support as a daily way of life, and has a special love and place in her heart for her many coworkers and friends; and WHEREAS, Mrs. Vaughn is the loving mother of two chil- dren, Jimmy and Jennifer; and a devoted grandmother to Ethan; dur- ing her leisure time, she also enjoys gardening, traveling, reading, interior design, and photography; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That upon the occasion of her retirement, April 1, 2006, and in recognition of her many outstanding professional achievements, highest com- mendation is hereby extended to Mrs. Rhoda Vaughn of Bir- mingham, Alabama, for whom a copy of this resolution shall be pro- vided with sincere regard and best wishes for every future happiness and success. Senator Poole requested and received unanimous consent to suspend the provisions of Senate Rule 55 and the Resolution was adopted by the Senate.

INVITING GOVERNOR JOE MANCHIN, III, OF WEST VIRGINIA TO ADDRESS A JOINT SESSION TO DIS- CUSS MINE SAFETY. WHEREAS, Governor Joe Manchin, III, of West Virginia, in conjunction with the Legislature of West Virginia, has successfully crafted and enacted landmark mine safety legislation; and 834 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2006 15th Day - February 23, 2006 WHEREAS, this far-reaching legislation includes requiring extra oxygen to be stored in mines, electrical tracking devices to be worn by miners, and the creation of a Mine and Industrial Accident Rapid Response System; and WHEREAS, like West Virginia, Alabama is a major coal mining state, and our miners daily risk their lives to heat and light our homes and businesses, and it is imperative that Alabama mines oper- ate in a safe manner and that the health and well-being of our miners are protected; and WHEREAS, Alabama coal mines are an essential state indus- try and play a critical role in the nation’s economic, energy, and homeland security policies; and WHEREAS, recent events in Alabama mines have led to clo- sures due to flooding and air quality problems, and prior tragic fatal- ities in state mines demand that we consider recent advancements and refinements in mine safety methods; and WHEREAS, the recent reforms enacted in West Virginia are of utmost interest to us, and it is appropriate to seek first-hand exper- tise regarding how Alabama should address this paramount issue; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That we respectfully extend an invitation to Governor Joe Manchin, III, of West Virginia, to address a Joint Session of the Alabama Legislature regarding mine safety on a date and time to be mutually arranged. A copy of this resolution shall be forwarded to Governor Manchin so that he may know of this invitation and our sincere hope that he may so honor us. Senator Poole requested and received unanimous consent to suspend the provisions of Senate Rule 55 and the Resolution was adopted by the Senate.

MOURNING THE DEATH OF MR. TERRY DIX- ON LANE. WHEREAS, it is with great sorrow and regret that we note the lamentable death of Mr. Terry Dixon Lane, a native of Letohatchee, Alabama, and resident of Montgomery, Alabama, on August 27, 2005, at the age of 62 years; and WHEREAS, Mr. Lane attended Auburn University and earned a Bachelor of Science Degree from Troy State University; and WHEREAS, he was employed by the Alabama Department of Revenue in 1968 and carried out his many duties and responsibil- ities in a highly efficient manner in numerous capacities including Assistant Supervisor of the Motor Vehicle Division’s Title Section, where he was instrumental in drafting legislation and implementing the Alabama Certificate of Title and Antitheft Act; and WHEREAS, with the interest of his fellow citizens always a priority, Mr. Lane worked tirelessly as Director of the Motor Vehicle Division before his death to help create the Mandatory Liability Insurance Act, a Legislative Oversight Committee on License Plates, organize a Motor Carrier Services Section, and on numerous other projects to improve the processing of title applications; and WHEREAS, he also was a faithful member of Sandy Ridge Methodist Church and an active member of the American Associa- tion of Motor Vehicle Administrators, the International Association of Automobile Theft Investigators, and the Alabama Cattlemen’s Association; and WHEREAS, left to cherish the memory of Mr. Lane are his loving wife, Jane Turnipseed Lane; sons, Jay P. Lane and James W. B. Lane; daughter-in-law, Kay Hayes Lane; and other devoted family members and friends; now therefore, REGULAR SESSION 1025 17th Day - March 2, 2006 BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH SIDES THEREOF CONCURRING, That the mem- ory of Mr. Terry Dixon Lane of Montgomery, Alabama, will live for- ever in the hearts and minds of all those whose lives he touched and it is directed that a copy of this resolution be presented to his wife with our sincere condolence. NAMING HIGHWAY 17 NORTH FROM HIGH- WAY 22 TO THE MONTEVALLO CITY LIMITS THE WAYNE DAVIS MEMORIAL HIGHWAY. WHEREAS, it is with great pride and admiration that the Ala- bama Legislature names Highway 17 North from Highway 22 to the Montevallo City Limits in honor of Wayne Davis, who lost his battle with cancer on January 24, 2006; and WHEREAS, Mr. Davis had lived on the same farm for 54 years, which was located on Highway 17 North in Montevallo, Ala- bama, and, as a tireless worker for good causes, he was a faithful Dea- con of the Montevallo First Baptist Church for more than 20 years; and was instrumental in establishing the first volunteer rescue service in Shelby County, where he served as a volunteer fireman, EMT, and Board member; and WHEREAS, over the years, he was blessed with the capabil- ity of a man who supported youth athletics by serving as a Youth League President, Commissioner, and Coach, as well as President of the Montevallo High School Athletic Booster Club until his untimely death; and WHEREAS, in a continuation of his outstanding achieve- ments, he provided equipment and assistance with the construction of a playground at the Montevallo Elementary School; served on the Montevallo Planning and Zoning Board; and was the owner and oper- ator of a construction business in Montevallo, where his professional 1034 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2006 17th Day - March 2, 2006 talents and expertise are evidenced in numerous church and city projects; and WHEREAS, it is befitting that Highway 17 North from High- way 22 to the Montevallo City Limits be named the Wayne Davis Memorial Highway as an enduring and lasting tribute; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That High- way 17 North from Highway 22 to the Montevallo City Limits be named the Wayne Davis Memorial Highway and it is directed that the appropriate authorities are encouraged to erect and maintain signs and markers specifying this designation of honor. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That a copy of this resolu- tion be provided to the family of Mr. Wayne Davis and the Depart- ment of Transportation, so that this meritorious designation is known. Senator Erwin requested and received unanimous consent to suspend the provisions of Senate Rule 55 and the Resolution was adopted by the Senate.

To provide for salary increases for certain officers em- ployed by the Department of Public Safety. The Standing Committee on Finance and Taxation General Fund reported the following substitute for the Bill, SB85, to wit: SUBSTITUTE FOR SB85 A BILL TO BE ENTITLED AN ACT To provide for salary increases for certain officers employed by the Department of Public Safety. BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALABAMA: Section 1. (a) Effective with the first payday on or after June 1, 2006, state troopers and corporals and such other comparable clas- sifications of arresting officers employed by the Department of Pub- lic Safety shall receive a four step, 10 percent, salary increase; ser- geants and lieutenants and such other comparable classifications of arresting officers employed by the department shall receive a three step, seven and one-half percent, salary increase; and captains and higher ranking officers and such other comparable classifications of arresting officers employed by the department shall receive a two step, five percent, salary increase. The salary increases provided herein shall not affect normal annual merit raise considerations. (b) The Director of the State Personnel Department shall re- vise the classifications and the schedule of rates set forth in the pay plan for employees employed by the Department of Public Safety to reflect the increases provided in subsection (a) and shall send the re- vised classifications and pay plan to the State Comptroller, who shall issue warrants in accordance therewith.

COMMENDING CAROL PAPPAS ON BEING ELECTED PRESIDENT OF THE ALABAMA PRESS ASSOCIA- TION. WHEREAS, highest commendations are herein extended to Carol Pappas on being elected President of the Alabama Press Asso- ciation representing more than 100 daily and weekly newspapers across the state; and WHEREAS, editor and publisher of The Daily Home and St. Clair Times, Carol Pappas is a 1977 graduate of Auburn University; she worked for two weeklies and in freelance before joining the staff of The Daily Home as a reporter in the newspaper’s Pell City Bureau; she has served as Bureau Manager, City Editor, Managing Editor, General Manager, and Publisher of both The Daily Home and St. Clair Times, the paper’s weekly publication for St. Clair County; and WHEREAS, the numerous civic activities of Carol Pappas include the Pell City Kiwanis, Talladega Kiwanis, Leadership Pell City, Leadership Talladega, Leadership Sylacauga, President of the St. Clair County Auburn Club, and Chairwoman of the Advisory Board of Pittard School of Technology in the Talladega County School System; and REGULAR SESSION 1263 20th Day - March 14, 2006 WHEREAS, a graduate of Leadership Alabama, Carol Pap- pas is Secretary of the Journalism Advisory Council at Auburn Uni- versity and Past President of Alabama Associated Press Managing Editors; and WHEREAS, the tireless work and exemplary leadership of Carol Pappas have been invaluable and she has made a lasting impression on those countless individuals with whom she has been associated; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That Carol Pappas is honored, commended, and recognized as the President of the Alabama Press Association and a copy of this resolution shall be provided for appropriate presentation with our sincere tribute and praise. RECOGNIZING THE BRUNDIDGE HISTORI- CAL SOCIETY’S “COME HOME, IT’S SUPPERTIME” AS ALA- BAMA’S ORIGINAL AND OFFICIAL FOLKLIFE PLAY. WHEREAS, the Brundidge Historical Society’s “Come Home, It’s Suppertime” is hereby recognized as Alabama’s Original and Official Folklife Play; and WHEREAS, in the spring of 2002, the Brundidge Historical Society presented the premier production of its “Come Home, It’s Suppertime”; the play was the realization of an eight-year dream of not only bringing community theater to Brundidge, but preserving the historic city hall building where the play is presented as the corner- stone of the town; and WHEREAS, the historic city hall building was constructed in 1940 as a Works Progress Administration project, and dubbed We Piddle Around because some believed that the WPA workers piddled around instead of working; it was gutted by fire in the early 1990s and has been magically turned into a unique community theater now known as the “We Piddle Around Theater”; and WHEREAS, centered around the Great Depression era, the play, from the original script, tells the story of the hardships, strug- gles, and perseverance of the people who lived during “Hoover Days” in a delightful, entertaining way; the stories are told by those who lived them and the original music is coupled with period songs and traditional hymns; there have been over 68 sold-out performanc- es; groups come from as far as Birmingham and Atlanta to see an unforgettable performance and dine on fried chicken, sweet ’taters, peas, turnips, cornbread, and blackberry pie; and WHEREAS, “Come Home, It’s Suppertime” is a unique sup- per theater experience and has brought great recognition to this small South Alabama town and brings all ages, races, and religions together to tell the story of a community; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That Senator Wendell Mitchell and Representative Alan Boothe join the Alabama Legislature in recognizing the Brundidge Historical Society’s Folk- life Play, “Come Home, It’s Suppertime,” as Alabama’s Original and REGULAR SESSION 1473 23rd Day - March 28, 2006 Official Folklife Play and do request the appropriate officials to place and maintain signs or markers recognizing this play. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That a copy of this resolu- tion be provided for appropriate presentation so that this meritorious designation is known. RECOGNIZING THE NAMING OF THE ALA- BAMA NATIONAL GUARD ARMORY AT FORT MCCLELLAN IN HONOR OF MAJOR GENERAL C. MARK BOWEN. WHEREAS, it is with great pride and pleasure that we recog- nize the naming of the Alabama National Guard Armory at Fort McClellan in honor of Major General C. Mark Bowen, who has served with distinction in the Alabama National Guard for more than 44 years, including service as Adjutant General since January 20, 2003; and WHEREAS, General Bowen has used his training and expe- rience to serve his country both as an enlisted soldier and officer and, throughout his career, he has placed an unwavering emphasis on pro- REGULAR SESSION 1547 23rd Day - March 28, 2006 viding leadership and service for Alabama’s Guard members, their families, and their employers; and WHEREAS, General Bowen was appointed by Governor Riley to command the mobilization of more than 10,000 Alabama National Guard members in the Global War on Terrorism, and he commanded an additional 5,000 Guard members during the 2004 and 2005 hurricane seasons; and WHEREAS, this Alabama son has indeed served his country as a warrior in combat and as a leader in peace as a citizen-soldier; and WHEREAS, it is the desire of the City of Anniston, the Cal- houn County Commission, and numerous veterans’ groups in the Calhoun County Community that the Alabama Armory Commission name the new Alabama National Guard Armory at the Fort McClel- lan Army National Guard Training Site the Fort C. Mark Bowen Armory in honor of Major General C. Mark Bowen; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That it is with highest commendation that we recognize the naming of the new Alabama National Guard Armory at the Fort McClellan Army National Guard Training Site as the Fort C. Mark Bowen Armory in honor of Major General C. Mark Bowen, and direct that a copy of this resolution be provided to him with tribute and esteem. MOURNING THE DEATH OF MRS. MARY ANN HALL. WHEREAS, herein recorded with deepest sorrow and regret is the death of Mrs. Mary Ann Hall of Gurley, Alabama, wife of our friend and colleague, Representative Albert Hall, on March 19, 2006; and WHEREAS, Mrs. Hall attended Calhoun Community Col- lege and The University of Alabama, earning a Registered Nurse Degree and beginning a 30-year nursing career at the Huntsville Hos- pital, and later with Home Health Care, where, with her infectious smile and contagious personality, she treated her patients with joy, compassion, and understanding, including bringing home-bound patients lunch from their favorite restaurant or supplying them with additional medical or personal supplies; and WHEREAS, Mrs. Hall was a warm and gracious lady who possessed a sweet spirit and had a genuine love for people all of her life; she especially enjoyed eating out, shopping, and traveling with REGULAR SESSION 1807 26th Day - April 4, 2006 her devoted granddaughter, Jessica Paige Curington, who, after she began driving, would bring breakfast to her grandmother on her way to school; and WHEREAS, Mrs. Hall also was a member of the Baptist Church and known for her charismatic personality, which quickly won the hearts of the members of her bridge group, as well as count- less others with whom she was associated; and WHEREAS, indeed, Mrs. Hall had warm and understanding ways, kindly wisdom, and a loving heart which entitled her to the gratitude and devotion of all those who loved her; and WHEREAS, left to cherish the memory of Mrs. Hall are her devoted husband of 48 years, Representative Albert Hall; daughter, Mary Lynda Hall; son, James “Jim” Hall; granddaughter, Jessica Paige Curington; and other loving family members and friends; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That heart- felt sympathy is extended to the husband of Mrs. Mary Ann Hall of Gurley, Alabama, whose sorrow we share, and for whom a copy of this resolution is provided with our sincere condolence.
